Fairfax County by the numbers

What kind of county is Fairfax County, Virginia?

Fairfax County is the most populous county in Virginia, a mostly suburban jurisdiction across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C. The 2020 census counted 1,150,309 residents.

It covers 406 square miles, of which about 391 are land. Montgomery County, Maryland sits to the north, and the county also touches Falls Church, Alexandria, Arlington County, Prince William County and Loudoun County. Wikipedia describes it as predominantly suburban with some urban and rural pockets.

ItemWhat the sources show
Formed1742, from part of Prince William County
Named forThomas Fairfax, 6th Lord Fairfax of Cameron
Total area406 square miles (391 land)
2020 census population1,150,309
Governing bodyTen-member Board of Supervisors plus an appointed county executive
School systemFairfax County Public Schools

Why is the county seat not inside Fairfax County?

The City of Fairfax is the county seat, but under Virginia law it is an independent city and is not part of the county. Falls Church and Alexandria are independent cities too, which is why a Fairfax County tax bill never covers a house inside those city limits.

Falls Church became independent in 1948 and the City of Fairfax in 1961, according to the county's Wikipedia history. For a seller this matters on day one. A house with a Fairfax mailing address might be billed by the county or by the City of Fairfax, or carry a Town of Herndon charge on top of the county. Check the name on the bill before you call anyone.

The Town of Herndon is a useful example. Fairfax County's Department of Tax Administration has collected Herndon's current real estate tax since a March 8, 2022 agreement, so Herndon owners get one bill that carries both the county and the town charge.

How did the county start, and how is it run?

Fairfax County was formed in 1742 from the northern part of Prince William County and takes its name from Thomas Fairfax, the proprietor of the Northern Neck. George Washington built Mount Vernon here, and Fort Belvoir sits partly on the old Belvoir estate.

Voters approved the urban county executive form of government in a 1966 referendum. Nine supervisors come from single-member districts (Braddock, Dranesville, Franconia, Hunter Mill, Mason, Mount Vernon, Providence, Springfield and Sully), and the chairman is elected countywide. The clerk of the circuit court, the sheriff and the commonwealth's attorney are separate elected officers.

Federal growth during and after World War II spurred rapid growth in the county, according to Wikipedia.

What drives the Fairfax County economy?

Professional services and technology carry the Fairfax County economy, and government is the largest employer. Fort Belvoir is the single largest source of federal jobs in the county.

  • Four U.S. intelligence agencies have headquarters here: the CIA at Langley, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency at Fort Belvoir, the National Reconnaissance Office in Chantilly and the National Counterterrorism Center in McLean.
  • Wikipedia lists Airbus, Volkswagen Group of America, Hilton Worldwide, Northrop Grumman, Leidos, Booz Allen Hamilton, Capital One and Freddie Mac among major employers, and counts eleven Fortune 500 headquarters.
  • Tysons is Virginia's largest office market. The Silver Line added four Metro stations there.

The county's 2020 median household income of $127,866 ranked fifth-highest in the country, per Wikipedia.

What is the Fairfax County real estate tax rate?

The county lists the 2026 base real estate rate at $1.12 per $100 of assessed value, shown as the proposed rate from the FY 2027 adopted budget. The same page shows $1.1225 for 2025 and $1.125 for 2024.

At $1.12, a house assessed at $700,000 would carry $7,840 a year in base tax, or $3,920 per installment, before any district charges. That is arithmetic from the published rate, not a bill, so use the figures on your own notice.

Not every parcel pays the same extra charges. The county says to find your parcel's tax district number in its assessment lookup, then match it against the 2026 rate chart. The Board of Supervisors sets the general rate in early May each year.

Which Fairfax County districts add to the bill?

Several service districts and service charges can sit on top of the base rate, and the assessment notice shows which ones apply to a parcel.

Charge2026 amount
Tysons Service District$0.05 per $100
Reston Service District$0.021 per $100
Stormwater Service District$0.0325 per $100
McLean Community Center$0.023 per $100
Reston Community Center$0.047 per $100
Lake Barcroft Watershed Improvement District$0.1107 per $100
Leaf collection (some districts)$0.019 per $100
Refuse fee (some districts)$630 per dwelling unit
Town of Herndon$0.27 per $100

The county also lists a $959 yearly charge for Springfield Water Service District 3, which runs through December 31, 2032 and serves a small group of homes in the Lincoln-Lewis-Vannoy Conservation District. Commercial transportation and Dulles Rail districts apply to commercial property, not to a typical house.

When are Fairfax County real estate taxes due?

Fairfax County bills real estate tax in two installments: July 28 and December 5. When a due date lands on a weekend or county holiday, it moves to the next business day, so the second 2026 installment is due Monday, December 7, 2026.

  • End of February: Notice of Real Estate Assessment Change mailed. In 2026 mailing began February 17.
  • April 1: deadline for an appeal to the Department of Tax Administration.
  • June 1: deadline for an appeal to the Board of Equalization.
  • July 28: first installment due. Bills go out by June 30.
  • December 5: second installment due. Bills go out by November 5.

The county states that taxes must be paid on time or penalties and interest apply, even when an appeal is pending. The pages reviewed did not list the penalty percentage, so ask the office for the current figure.

How do you appeal a Fairfax County assessment?

There are three levels, and the first two have firm 2026 dates. The assessment effective date is January 1, and the county reported an average residential increase of 3.99% for 2026.

  1. Department of Tax Administration review. File by April 1 (postmarked, or 4:30 p.m. if online or by email). Mail goes to 12000 Government Center Parkway, Suite 357, Fairfax, VA 22035.
  2. Board of Equalization, an independent panel appointed by the Board of Supervisors. File by June 1. Its decisions are final but can be taken to circuit court.
  3. Fairfax County Circuit Court, through an Application for Correction of Erroneous Assessment under Virginia Code 58.1-3984.

The county says an appeal needs a basis in fair market value, lack of uniformity or an error in the property description. Saying the increase is too large in one year is not a legal basis. For a house, bring sales of similar homes or comparables. An agent filing for you needs a signed, notarized authorization letter.

Appraisal staff take calls at 703-222-8234 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

What happens to unpaid Fairfax County tax when a house sells?

Unpaid real estate tax follows the house, because Virginia gives the tax lien priority over other liens until the tax is actually paid. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 says the lien comes ahead of any other lien or encumbrance, and that the proceeds of a sale must be applied to taxes and levies on the real estate. It also covers the penalties and interest, and puts a further lien on the rents for the current year.

The same section says the seller's share of the taxes is prorated by contract. If installments are unpaid at closing, ask the settlement agent how the balance will be handled on the closing statement.

Recordation also has a seller-side cost. Virginia Code 58.1-802 imposes a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of consideration on a deed, paid by the grantor unless the parties agree that the buyer pays some or all of it. The consideration has to be stated on the first page of the deed.

What relief exists for Fairfax County owners and damaged houses?

Fairfax County runs tax relief for seniors age 65 and older and for people with disabilities, and exemptions for disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses. Returning applicants renew by May 1, and first-time or hardship applicants can apply through December 31 for the current and one prior year.

A damaged or decayed house has its own route. The county can adjust the assessment when a building is wholly destroyed, or reduced in value below $100 by decay, or impaired by violence by $100 or more, under Virginia Code 58.1-3293. Any adjustment is prorated from the incident until the repair or the end of the year. Send the address or tax map number, a description of the damage, repair estimates if you have them and photographs to the Department of Tax Administration at 703-222-8234.

More questions about Fairfax County, VA Property Tax Guide

Is Fairfax County property tax paid once or twice a year?

Twice a year. The first installment is due July 28 and the second December 5, moved to Monday, December 7 in 2026 because December 5 falls on a Saturday.

What is the Fairfax County base real estate tax rate?

The county lists $1.12 per $100 of assessed value for tax year 2026, shown as the proposed rate in the FY 2027 adopted budget. Your notice shows any district charges on top.

Can I appeal my Fairfax County assessment after I list the house?

The 2026 administrative deadline was April 1 and the Board of Equalization deadline was June 1, so those windows have closed for this year. Ask the Department of Tax Administration about the next cycle, and keep paying on time while any appeal is pending.

Who collects tax for the Town of Herndon?

Fairfax County's Department of Tax Administration does, under a March 8, 2022 agreement. Herndon owners receive one combined bill for county and town real estate tax.

Does the buyer or the seller pay the Virginia grantor's tax?

The seller, as grantor, pays it unless both sides agree that the buyer covers some or all of it. The rate under Virginia Code 58.1-802 is 50 cents for each $500 of consideration.

Who do I call about a Fairfax County assessment?

The Department of Tax Administration, Real Estate Division, at 703-222-8234 or DTARED@fairfaxcounty.gov. The office is at 12000 Government Center Parkway, Suite 357, Fairfax, VA 22035.

Loudoun County by the numbers

Where is Loudoun County, Virginia, and why is it growing?

Loudoun County is a northern Virginia county on the Potomac River, across from Maryland, and it is part of the Washington metropolitan area. Leesburg is the county seat and its largest town.

The county covers 521 square miles. Its 2020 population of 420,959 made it the third most populous county in Virginia, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 449,749. The Bull Run and Catoctin mountains cut through it, with the Loudoun Valley to the west and the Blue Ridge forming the western edge.

Growth came fast. The county had 86,129 residents in 1990, 169,599 in 2000 and 312,311 in 2010. Sellers here often own houses that were built in the last few decades, though the western towns hold much older homes.

What is the history of Loudoun County?

Loudoun County was formed in 1757 from Fairfax County and named for John Campbell, the Fourth Earl of Loudoun and governor general of Virginia. English and Welsh Quakers, Scots-Irish and German settlers arrived from Pennsylvania and Maryland starting in the 1720s and 1730s.

By the Revolution it was Virginia's most populous county and grew so much grain that it earned the nickname Breadbasket of the Revolution. President James Monroe lived at Oak Hill from 1823 until his death in 1831.

The Civil War divided the county. The Battle of Ball's Bluff was fought near Leesburg on October 21, 1861, and cavalry clashed at Aldie, Middleburg and Upperville in June 1863. The county's population then sat near 20,000 for a century. In 1962 Dulles International Airport opened in the southeast, and the high-tech boom that followed pulled eastern Loudoun into the Washington suburbs.

Which Loudoun County towns and communities matter to sellers?

Loudoun has seven incorporated towns: Hamilton, Hillsboro, Leesburg, Lovettsville, Middleburg, Purcellville and Round Hill. A house inside a town sits under town government as well as the county, so ask the town office about any local rules that apply to your street.

The large census-designated places in the east include Ashburn, South Riding, Sterling, Brambleton, Broadlands, Stone Ridge, Lansdowne, Sugarland Run, Cascades, Lowes Island and Countryside. Wikipedia's 2018 estimates put Leesburg at 52,125 people and Ashburn at 50,290. Smaller places such as Waterford, Aldie, Bluemont and Lucketts anchor the rural west.

The split matters when you price and market a house. The eastern planned communities are made up of recent subdivisions, and the Loudoun Valley mixes villages, farms and horse properties. Each sells differently, and a cash buyer will weigh the condition of the roof, septic or well on a rural lot differently from a townhouse on public utilities.

What drives the Loudoun County economy?

Loudoun's economy rests on technology, aviation, government and agriculture. Wikipedia reports that the county holds more than 60 large data centers in an area known as Data Center Alley, with over 25 million square feet, the world's largest concentration.

According to the county's financial reports, the top employers in 2024 were:

  • Loudoun County Public Schools, 12,968 employees
  • County of Loudoun, 4,813 employees
  • U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Inova Health System and United Airlines, each 2,500 to 5,000
  • Amazon, Northrop Grumman, Verizon Business, RTX and Walmart, each 1,000 to 2,500

Farming has not gone away. The county has about 40 wineries, more than 25 active farms and an equine industry estimated at $78 million. Wikipedia also states that the median household income in 2023 was $156,821, the highest of any county in the nation. High incomes do not protect every household from a hardship, though, and a job loss, divorce or inherited property still pushes owners to sell quickly.

How do roads and transit affect Loudoun County homes?

Major roads include U.S. 15, U.S. 50 and U.S. 340, plus State Routes 7, 9, 28 and 267, the Dulles Greenway. Loudoun County Parkway and Braddock Road also carry local traffic.

The county has two airports, Dulles International and Leesburg Executive, and runs its own bus system, Loudoun County Transit. The Washington Metro Silver Line serves the Dulles Airport, Loudoun Gateway and Ashburn stations. Proximity to a Metro station, a toll road or an airport flight path is something a buyer's agent will bring up, so note it when you describe the house.

Which schools serve Loudoun County?

Loudoun County Public Schools serves more than 70,000 students and is the fifth largest school system in Virginia. The county also sends students to the Loudoun Academy of Science, now part of the Academies of Loudoun, and is eligible to send students to Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology.

Private options include Loudoun Country Day School, Notre Dame Academy in Middleburg, and Foxcroft School. Higher education includes Patrick Henry College and a Northern Virginia Community College campus in Sterling. A seller should confirm attendance zones with the school division and not rely on a listing.

How does Loudoun County real estate tax work?

In Loudoun County, the Commissioner of the Revenue handles assessments and the Treasurer handles billing and collection. The elected Clerk of the Circuit Court records deeds. We could not open the county's own tax pages for this guide, so we are not giving Loudoun's current rate, installment dates or appeal deadline. Call the offices to confirm.

State law gives you tools that apply in every county. A person who thinks an assessment is wrong because of a clerical or factual error can apply to the assessing officer for a correction within three years of the end of the tax year, or one year from the assessment date, whichever is later. That route is for errors made by the assessing office or caused by factual mistakes during a general reassessment. See Virginia Code 58.1-3980.

For a dispute over value, the board of equalization route applies, and the rule is that the assessor's value is presumed correct. The board may consider market sales through the December 31 before the assessment date if they are filed by the locality's deadline.

What help exists if a Loudoun County owner is behind on tax?

A locality may by resolution grant reasonable extensions of up to 90 days for real estate tax when good cause exists. State law also requires an automatic extension on a primary residence for service members deployed outside the United States, ending 90 days after deployment ends.

Where omitted taxes have been assessed, the Treasurer can be authorized to arrange a payment plan of up to 72 months, provided current taxes are paid as they come due. Penalty cannot exceed 10 percent of the tax past due, and interest cannot exceed 10 percent a year initially.

If the house is a rental, inherited or needs work, a written cash offer from Cash Home Buyers can give you a clear number to compare against the cost of repairs and a listing. There is no obligation to accept.

Who sets real estate assessments in Loudoun County?

The Commissioner of the Revenue's office handles assessments, while the Treasurer bills and collects. Confirm current dates and the appeal deadline with both offices, because we could not verify them online.

How big is Loudoun County, Virginia?

The county covers 521 square miles and had 420,959 residents in the 2020 census, making it Virginia's third most populous county.

Is Loudoun County mostly owner-occupied?

Yes. The 2020 census shows 76.4 percent of occupied housing units were owner-occupied and 23.6 percent were rented.

Can I get a Loudoun County property tax penalty removed?

Virginia law bars penalty and interest when the failure to pay was not the taxpayer's fault, such as certain postal errors. Ask the Treasurer, who decides fault for late payments.

Which Metro stations are in Loudoun County?

The Silver Line serves the Dulles Airport, Loudoun Gateway and Ashburn stations inside the county.

Prince William County by the numbers

Where is Prince William County, VA, and how is it laid out?

Prince William County sits on the Potomac River in Northern Virginia and covers 348 square miles, of which 336 are land. Loudoun and Fairfax Counties border it on the north, Fauquier on the west and Stafford on the south, with Charles County, Maryland, across the river (Wikipedia).

The county seat is Manassas, an independent city that sits inside the county. Manassas Park is a second independent city enclosed by it. A house in either city is billed by the city, not by the county, so check the town on the deed before you look up a tax account.

The county elects seven supervisors by magisterial district (Brentsville, Coles, Potomac, Gainesville, Neabsco, Occoquan and Woodbridge) plus an at-large chair. Incorporated towns are Dumfries, Haymarket, Occoquan and Quantico. Dale City is the largest community, and Woodbridge, Lake Ridge, Gainesville and Linton Hall are census-designated places. The western half is a green belt called the rural crescent, which matters if your parcel is larger than a subdivision lot.

Which Prince William County offices handle real estate tax?

Two county offices split the work: the Real Estate Assessments Office sets the value and Taxpayer Services handles bills and payments, both under Tax Administration.

OfficeWhat it doesContact on the county page
Real Estate Assessments OfficeValues property, answers assessment questions, takes correction requests703-792-6780, realestate@pwcgov.org, 4379 Ridgewood Center Drive, Suite 203, Prince William, VA 22192
Taxpayer ServicesBilling and payment questions703-792-6710, TaxpayerServices@pwcgov.org
Board of EqualizationHears real estate assessment appeals after the office reviewAppeal form posted on the county site

The county lists in-person assessment office hours as Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and phone hours as 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Payments are made through the county's Taxpayer Portal. The county also warns against mailing checks because of check washing fraud and suggests paying online (Prince William County real estate tax page).

When is Prince William County real estate tax due?

Prince William County bills real estate tax in two installments a year, and county notices show the first half due July 15 and the second half due December 5.

  • First half of 2026: due July 15, 2026, according to the county's June 22 notice.
  • Second half of 2025: due December 5, 2025.
  • Second half of 2024 and 2022: also due December 5 in the county's notices for those years.

The county's notice page did not show a December 2026 notice when we looked, so confirm the second-half date for this year with Taxpayer Services before you plan a closing around it. Most owners with a mortgage pay through escrow. The county says it bills mortgage servicing companies directly, and if you get a paper bill that your servicer should have received, you are asked to forward it to the servicer (county tax news).

The county also charges a supplemental real estate tax on new improvements finished after the start of the year. A seller who built an addition or finished a basement recently should ask whether a supplemental bill is still coming.

How does Prince William County calculate the real estate tax bill?

The bill is the assessed value divided by 100 and multiplied by the total rate, which the county states per $100 of value.

The Board of County Supervisors sets a county-wide base rate each year, a Fire and Rescue levy, a Mosquito and Forest Pest Management levy, and special district levies that pay for things such as road improvements. Storm water management and solid waste fees are set separately. The county's own worked example uses a rate of $0.9805 per $100 and an assessed value of $607,800, which gives $5,959.48. That figure is an illustration from the county page, not this year's rate, so use the rate on your own bill.

  • Check which special district levies apply to your address.
  • Add storm water and solid waste fees if they appear on the bill.
  • Ask about any supplemental bill for new construction.

How do I challenge a Prince William County assessment?

Start with the Real Estate Assessments Office, then go to the Board of Equalization, and use the circuit court if you still disagree.

The county's Taxpayer Bill of Rights says owners can examine the working papers behind a value, meet with assessment staff, and request a correction if they think the value is wrong or unfair. It also lists appeals to the Board of Equalization for real estate and to the circuit court (county rights page). The county posts a Board of Equalization appeal form each year, but we could not open its text, so we do not state a deadline here. Read the notice you received and ask the office.

Virginia law sets the ground rules. The board starts from a presumption that the assessor's value is correct, and the owner must show by a preponderance of the evidence that the property is valued above fair market value or that the assessment is not uniform (Va. Code 58.1-3379). Sales and income evidence up to December 31 before the assessment date can be considered. Separately, a taxpayer can ask the assessing official to correct an erroneous assessment within three years of the end of the tax year or one year from the assessment, whichever is later, but that route covers errors by the assessor, not disagreements over opinion of value (Va. Code 58.1-3980).

What happens to unpaid Prince William County property tax when I sell?

Unpaid real estate tax follows the house, because Virginia gives the tax a lien ahead of every other lien until it is paid.

State law says the purchaser at a sale, or the trustee in a foreclosure sale, must cause the sale proceeds to be applied to all taxes assessed on the real estate, and that taxes include penalties and interest. The seller's share of the year is prorated by contract, and the treasurer or other proper officer releases the lien (Va. Code 58.1-3340). In practice, the closing agent pays what is owed from the seller's proceeds. Ask Taxpayer Services for a payoff figure that includes the current half before the closing date is set.

The deed also carries a state grantor's tax of 50 cents for each $500 of consideration, paid by the seller unless the contract shifts it to the buyer, and the clerk will not record the deed until it is paid (Va. Code 58.1-802). Prince William County, Manassas and Manassas Park share one Circuit Court clerk, so recording questions for all three go to the same office.

What do sellers in Prince William County usually face?

Most sellers here own their homes and deal with a commuter market tied to Washington, D.C., military employers and a fast-growing tax base.

At the 2020 census the county had 158,525 housing units, 3.0 percent of them vacant, and 71.6 percent of occupied units were owner-occupied. Top employers in the county's 2025 annual financial report include Prince William County Public Schools, the county government, the Department of Defense, Walmart and Sentara Healthcare. The county is also home to Marine Corps Base Quantico and a large concentration of data centers shared with Loudoun County.

  • Commuting: Interstate 66 and Interstate 95 cross the county, along with U.S. 1, U.S. 15, U.S. 29 and State Route 234.
  • Transit: Virginia Railway Express runs a Manassas line and a Fredericksburg line, and PRTC provides OmniRide bus service.
  • Schools: Prince William County Public Schools is the second largest school system in Virginia, and Quantico is served by the Department of Defense Education Activity.

Sellers behind on payments, with inherited property, or with a house that needs work often prefer a direct cash sale because it avoids repair requests from retail buyers. A cash buyer still has to clear the tax lien at closing, so the same payoff steps apply.

More questions about Prince William County, VA Property Tax Guide

When is the first half of Prince William County real estate tax due in 2026?

July 15, 2026, according to the county's June 22, 2026 notice. The second half has been due December 5 in the notices we reviewed for 2022, 2024 and 2025, so confirm the 2026 date with Taxpayer Services.

Who do I call about a Prince William County assessment?

The Real Estate Assessments Office at 703-792-6780 or realestate@pwcgov.org. For billing and payment questions, call Taxpayer Services at 703-792-6710.

Can I sell my Prince William County house if I owe property tax?

Yes. The tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, because Virginia gives it priority over other liens. Get a payoff amount from Taxpayer Services so the closing agent can include penalties and interest.

Does Prince William County bill houses in Manassas?

No. Manassas and Manassas Park are independent cities surrounded by the county and bill their own real estate tax. Confirm the jurisdiction on your deed or bill.

What can I do if I think my Prince William County value is too high?

Ask the Real Estate Assessments Office to review it, then appeal to the Board of Equalization or the circuit court if needed. Under state law the owner must rebut a presumption that the assessor's value is correct, so bring sales or appraisal evidence.

Chesterfield County by the numbers

Where is Chesterfield County, Virginia?

Chesterfield County lies just south of Richmond, with the James River forming much of its northern border and the Appomattox River much of its southern one. The county seat is Chesterfield Court House, and the county has no incorporated towns.

It is large. The 2020 census counted 364,548 residents, the fourth most populous county in Virginia, and the county's 2025 estimate is 397,148. The county covers 437 square miles, of which 423 are land.

It crosses the Fall Line, with hillier Piedmont terrain to the west and flatter Tidewater coastal plain to the east. Neighbors include Henrico, Colonial Heights, Petersburg, Hopewell, Powhatan and Dinwiddie.

What is the history of Chesterfield County?

Chesterfield was created from part of Henrico County on May 25, 1749, and named for Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield. It has an unusually long record of firsts: coal mining began in the 1730s, the Manchester Turnpike opened in 1807 as Virginia's first graveled road of significant length, and the Chesterfield Railroad opened in 1831 as Virginia's first railroad.

Richmond annexed 23 square miles of the county in 1970 under the Horner-Bagley Compromise, and in 1981 Chesterfield gained immunity from further annexation by Richmond. After World War II the county grew quickly as a commuter suburb. That history explains why many Chesterfield houses are postwar and later subdivisions, with a few older farm properties scattered between them.

Which communities, roads and employers define Chesterfield County?

The best known communities are Chester, the largest, followed by Midlothian, Bon Air, Brandermill, Ettrick, Bermuda Hundred and Matoaca. The northern portion is often called North Chesterfield.

  • Interstate 95 runs through the county, and Interstate 85 begins near Petersburg.
  • U.S. 60 (Midlothian Turnpike) follows the route of the 1807 turnpike.
  • The Powhite Parkway extension (State Route 76) and the Pocahontas Parkway (State Route 895), an 8.8 mile toll road, cross the area.
  • GRTC Route 111 has linked the Chippenham Parkway area to Brightpoint Community College in Chester since March 2020.

Employers with 1,000 or more workers include Amazon Fulfillment Services, HCA Virginia Health System, UPS, Walmart, DuPont Specialty Products, Kroger, Bon Secours Richmond Health System, Food Lion and Capital One. Commonwealth Fusion Systems plans a grid-scale fusion power plant at the James River Industrial Center, and the county approved its conditional use permit in 2025.

What do sellers in Chesterfield County usually deal with?

The county's growth since World War II, when it became a commuter suburb of Richmond, means a large share of its houses are decades old. Original roofs, aging heating and cooling equipment and dated kitchens are common reasons a house sits unsold, and a buyer using a mortgage may ask for repairs that an as is cash buyer does not.

Chesterfield's size also matters. With more than 364,000 residents, an owner who inherits a house, or who has moved away, may be managing a property from far off while tax statements keep arriving. Getting the Treasurer's current balance early is a useful first step, and the county's payment plan page is worth reading before the next due date.

How does the Chesterfield assessment cycle work?

Chesterfield reassesses real estate every year. Assessment notices are mailed by February 1 and show values as of January 1, and the county says assessments must reflect 100 percent of fair market value.

The Board of Supervisors sets the tax rate, and the county lists $0.89 per $100 of assessed value for 2026. Values are based on inspections, sales data and comparisons with similar nearby properties. Commercial owners are asked to complete an income and expense survey online by July 15.

How do you appeal a Chesterfield County assessment?

File with Real Estate Assessments by March 15, then go to the Board of Equalization by April 15 if you disagree. The county says late applications are not processed, and that the first level is required before you can appeal further.

  1. Review your values on the county's READ site or contact the office.
  2. Get the application and file a separate one for each property.
  3. Attach support: up to three comparable properties, a recent appraisal or photos, and for income property three years of income and expense statements plus a current rent roll.
  4. If a representative files for you, add a notarized Letter of Authorization.
  5. An appraiser may ask questions or inspect, then notifies you of the outcome.

The Board of Equalization is an independent board under the Code of Virginia. Its members are appointed by a Circuit Court judge and trained by the Virginia Department of Taxation. Under 58.1-3379, the assessor's value is presumed correct and the owner must rebut it. Real Estate Assessments is at 6801 Mimms Loop, with phone 804-748-1321 and email assessor@chesterfield.gov.

What else shapes a Chesterfield County bill?

Geography decides which services and which mailing address apply, and it helps to know a few quirks before a sale. Ettrick, for example, is mostly served by a Petersburg mailing address even though it lies in Chesterfield County, so a seller there should check which locality actually bills the parcel. The county tax office, not the postal city, is the one to ask.

The Real Estate Assessments page also names a contact for the Lower Magnolia Green Community Development Authority, so ask the closing agent whether your parcel sits in a special district or carries a charge beyond the normal county bill.

  • Automated Payment Service: free, with taxes debited on the due date after about 30 to 45 days of activation.
  • APS returns: a $50 return-item fee applies for insufficient funds, in addition to any bank fees.
  • Citizen Portal: shows invoices for the most recent six years.
  • Payment kiosks: take cash, cards and checks, around the clock.

These details matter when an heir is cleaning up an old account. The six year view lets you see what was billed, and the Treasurer can explain anything older.

When are Chesterfield County real estate taxes due and how do you pay?

The county's homepage lists the current real estate tax as due Monday, December 7, 2026, and warns of a 10 percent penalty if it is missed. The Pay Your Taxes page we opened does not list the dates or the penalty rates, so confirm both with the Treasurer.

The Treasurer's Office is at 9901 Lori Road, Room 101, Chesterfield, VA 23832, with mail to P.O. Box 70. The phone is 804-748-1201, and hours are weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

  • Online through the Citizen Portal, which now requires an account.
  • By phone at 855-933-5661, around the clock.
  • Through your bank's bill pay, mailed to P.O. Box 70.
  • At payment kiosks in seven county library and administration locations.
  • By drop box at the Lane B. Ramsey Administration Building, checks or money orders only.

Processor fees are 2 percent for credit cards and a flat $2.50 for debit cards, while eCheck has no fee. Virginia's 58.1-3916 caps interest at 10 percent a year and the property penalty at 10 percent.

What can a Chesterfield seller do if the tax bill is behind?

A seller who cannot pay on time can apply for a tax payment plan through the county, though interest and fees keep accruing during the plan. The county says staff respond within two business days and that approval is not guaranteed.

A plan also does not release a DMV stop, which is lifted only when accounts are paid in full. That is worth knowing if you have both vehicle and real estate balances.

At closing, Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 under 58.1-802. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure that matches your closing date, since interest grows daily. March 15 for Real Estate Assessments, and April 15 for the Board of Equalization. The county does not process late applications.

Where is the Chesterfield County Treasurer?

At 9901 Lori Road, Room 101, Chesterfield, VA 23832. The phone is 804-748-1201 and the office is open weekdays, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Does a Chesterfield payment plan stop penalties?

No. The county says interest and fees keep accruing during a plan, and a plan does not release a DMV stop.

Can I sell a Chesterfield County house with back taxes?

Yes, the balance is normally paid from the proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before the closing date.

Henrico County by the numbers

Where is Henrico County, Virginia?

Henrico County curves around the City of Richmond on its west, north and east sides. The Chickahominy River forms the northern boundary, Tuckahoe Creek the western one, and the James River and Richmond lie to the south.

It covers 245 square miles. The 2020 census counted 334,389 people, which made it the fifth most populous county in Virginia, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 342,775. There is no incorporated town inside Henrico, so Laurel, an unincorporated census-designated place, serves as the seat of government.

More than a third of occupied homes here are rented. A Henrico County owner who sells a house that has been a rental often deals with tenants, deferred repairs, or both.

How old is Henrico County, and what happened here?

Henrico is one of the oldest counties in the United States. Thomas Dale founded the Citie of Henricus in 1611 on a peninsula in the James River, and in 1634 Henrico Shire became one of the eight original shires of Virginia. Ten counties and three independent cities were later formed from its territory, including Chesterfield, Albemarle, Goochland and Richmond itself.

Richmond became fully independent in 1842. The city later annexed pieces of Henrico five times, and in 1961 voters in Henrico rejected a merger by 61 percent. A 1965 attempt to annex 145 square miles ended with the city allowed only 17. Since the state's 1981 annexation moratorium, the county line has stayed put.

Several 1862 Peninsula Campaign battles, including Seven Pines and Malvern Hill, took place in Henrico, and J.E.B. Stuart was mortally wounded at Yellow Tavern in 1864. With a history that long, a Henrico County house can be almost any age, so ask for the year built before you compare it to a neighbor.

Which communities, roads and transit serve Henrico County?

The census-designated places are Chamberlayne, Dumbarton, East Highland Park, Glen Allen, Highland Springs, Innsbrook, Lakeside, Laurel, Montrose, Sandston, Short Pump, Tuckahoe and Wyndham, with Fair Oaks and Varina as other named communities.

  • Interstates 64, 95, 195 and 295 all cross the county.
  • Richmond International Airport is in the eastern part of the county, at Sandston.
  • Amtrak's Richmond Staples Mill Road station is in Henrico.
  • The county buys bus service from the Greater Richmond Transit Company.

Henrico is also one of only two Virginia counties that maintain their own roads, along with Arlington, a status that grew from county highway departments that predate the state system. If a road next to your property needs attention, the answer comes from the county and not from the state highway agency.

What does the local economy look like in Henrico County?

Henrico's largest employers are Henrico County Public Schools and Capital One, each in the 5,000 to 9,999 range according to an older county financial report listed on Wikipedia. The same list shows Henrico County government, Henrico Doctors' Hospital, Anthem, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Walmart, the Postal Service, Genworth and Kroger in the 1,000 to 4,999 range.

Altria Group has had its headquarters in the county, and Wikipedia describes Henrico as a major data center hub. Lewis Ginter Botanical Garden and Richmond Raceway are also here. Wells Fargo's listing at Innsbrook shows that some of this employment sits in office parks inside the county.

The county's climate is humid subtropical. On average it sees 50 days above 90 degrees, 88 days with lows below freezing, and about 43 inches of precipitation a year, so roofs, gutters and crawl space moisture matter when a buyer's inspector visits.

How does Henrico County assess real estate?

Henrico assesses all real estate every year at 100 percent of fair market value, with each reassessment effective January 1. The Real Estate Assessment Division, part of the Department of Finance, works from recorded deeds and the sales prices reported by buyers, sellers and agents.

Staff compare sale prices with assessed values. A neighborhood is picked for reassessment when its ratio is well above or below 100 percent. For houses, the division generally uses the sales comparison approach, adjusting for size, quality, condition and location.

Notices of assessment are mailed beginning in February. Tax bills usually go straight to the mortgage company, so a homeowner with an escrow account may never see the notice unless the lender passes it along. The division's page is at henrico.gov.

How do you appeal a Henrico County assessment?

To contest a Henrico assessment, apply for reconsideration. By law the appeal must be filed no later than April 1 of the current year, and the division's page gives 804-501-4300 and AssessmentAppeal@henrico.gov for forms.

Reconsideration is warranted when the value exceeds fair market value, rests on incorrect property information, or is inequitable against similar properties. Staff inspect the property, notify the owner of a recommended value, and forward the case to the Board of Real Estate Review and Equalization. An owner who still disagrees may appear before the board.

At that hearing Virginia's burden rule applies, so bring comparable sales and evidence of condition. Under state law, a bill is not treated as delinquent while an administrative appeal filed within 90 days of the assessment is pending, plus 30 days after the final decision.

When are Henrico County real estate taxes due?

Henrico bills real estate and personal property tax in two installments, due on or before June 5 and December 5. These dates come from the Treasury Division, which issues the bills and collects the money under County Code section 20-108.

Treasury has two offices, at 4301 E. Parham Road and 3820 Nine Mile Road, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding holidays. It also collects delinquent real estate and personal property taxes.

The county lists these relief programs on the assessment page: partial exemptions for certain residential, multifamily and commercial properties, an exemption for qualified disabled veterans and their surviving spouses, the Real Estate Advantage Program for owners 65 or older or disabled with an April 1 filing deadline, and a Land Use program with a November 1 application date. Penalty and interest amounts should be confirmed with Treasury before you plan a payoff.

What should a Henrico County seller know about tax at closing?

If the house sells after a bill has been mailed, Virginia allows the treasurer to cancel the bill sent to the prior owner and reissue it to the new owner. No penalty applies to that reissued assessment if it is paid within two weeks after the notice is mailed.

A seller who is behind should get a payoff figure in writing from Treasury, with the date through which it is good. Cash Home Buyers can review a Henrico County house as is, including a rental with tenants or a house with unpaid tax, and send a written cash offer without obligation.

The first installment is due on or before June 5 and the second on or before December 5, according to the county Treasury Division.

Yes. The Real Estate Assessment Division reviews and reassesses all real property effective January 1 each year, and mails notices beginning in February.

Treasury has offices at 4301 E. Parham Road and 3820 Nine Mile Road, open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding holidays.

The county lists a Real Estate Advantage Program for owners who are 65 or older or disabled and who meet other criteria, with an April 1 filing deadline. Call 804-501-4263 for details.

Stafford County by the numbers

Where is Stafford County, Virginia, and how is it divided?

Stafford County lies on the Potomac and Rappahannock rivers in Northern Virginia, across the Rappahannock from the City of Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania County. It is part of the Washington metropolitan area, and it was created in 1664 from Westmoreland County and named for Staffordshire, England.

The county covers 280 square miles, of which 269 are land. Its seat is Stafford, and its largest community is Aquia Harbour. Wikipedia counts 156,927 residents in 2020 and a 2025 Census Bureau estimate of 170,803.

Stafford is run by a Board of Supervisors elected from seven magisterial districts, with a county administrator managing departments. The district names are a handy way to locate a property.

What does the 2020 census say about homes in Stafford County?

How do Quantico and federal jobs shape the Stafford housing market?

Marine Corps Base Quantico occupies part of northern Stafford County, and the FBI Academy, the FBI National Laboratory and NCIS headquarters sit on the Stafford side of the base. Wikipedia says many residents commute north to defense and federal sites, and that many military families live in the county.

If you are selling because of a transfer or a deployment, tell your closing agent your move date early so the settlement can be scheduled around it.

  • Residents commute by I-95, U.S. 1 and the Virginia Railway Express.
  • On-post addresses at Quantico are zoned to Department of Defense schools, not the county system.
  • Wikipedia ties the county's high household incomes to its federal and defense commuters.

What roads and rail lines serve Stafford County?

Interstate 95 is the backbone, and the southern end of the I-95 Express Lanes is in Stafford County, north of Exit 133. The extension to that point was fully completed in December 2023.

U.S. 1, U.S. 17 and State Routes 3, 212 and 218 are the other major roads. The VRE commuter rail has Leeland and Brooke stations in the county, and Stafford Regional Airport is also here. A 2017 INRIX study ranked southbound I-95 from Washington to the southern tip of Stafford as the worst single traffic hotspot in the nation.

Seller takeaway: describe the drive to the VRE station and the interstate in your listing, because buyers weigh the commute heavily here.

What severe weather has hit Stafford County homes?

A tornado touched down in southern Stafford County in the early hours of May 9, 2008, and damaged about 140 suburban homes. Heavy snow has also hit: roughly 25 inches fell in December 2009 and about 19 inches in February 2010.

Buyers sometimes ask about roof age, attic insulation and tree work after storms like these. Gather any storm repair receipts and roof invoices before you list.

  • Keep proof of roof replacement or patching.
  • Note any insurance claims paid on the house.
  • Trim trees near the roofline before showings.

What history do Stafford County's older properties carry?

Stafford has colonial roots and many sites on the National Register. George Washington spent much of his childhood at Ferry Farm, and Aquia Church, built in 1757, is a National Historic Landmark. Aquia Creek sandstone from Government Island was used to build the White House and the U.S. Capitol.

The Civil War also reached the county, and more than 100,000 troops occupied it repeatedly. In 1862 about 10,000 enslaved people crossed the Rappahannock to reach Union lines, a Trail of Freedom marked on both banks. Falmouth, the town beside Fredericksburg, was the home of painter Gari Melchers, whose house Belmont is listed on the National Register. If your house is in an older area such as Falmouth or Aquia, ask the county planning office whether any local review applies.

Which schools and colleges serve Stafford County?

Stafford County Public Schools serves most of the county, with six high schools: Brooke Point, Colonial Forge, Hartwood, Mountain View, North Stafford and Stafford Senior. Areas on Marine Corps Base Quantico go to Crossroads Elementary and Quantico Middle/High School.

Germanna Community College, Strayer University and the University of Mary Washington are nearby, and private schools include Holy Cross Academy, Merit School, Fredericksburg Christian School, Saint William of York Catholic School, Fredericksburg Academy and Grace Preparatory School. Buyers confirm school zones themselves, so point them to the school division instead of promising a zone.

How does a Stafford County real estate assessment appeal work?

You first ask the assessor to review the value, and if you disagree you can take the case to the Board of Equalization. The board presumes the assessor is right, and the owner must prove the home is valued above fair market value or was not assessed uniformly.

  • For a residential property with fewer than four units, you can ask in writing for the assessment records, and the assessing officer must deliver them within 15 days.
  • If the officer misses that deadline, the officer must present the records and explain the valuation method at the hearing before you speak.
  • Sales through December 31 before the assessment date may be used, and later studies cannot.
  • The board may raise or lower values, with or without a specific complaint.

Separately, errors made by the assessor or factual errors made during a general reassessment can be corrected by application within three years of the end of the tax year or one year of the assessment, whichever is later. Ask the Stafford County Commissioner of the Revenue for the local filing deadline, since we could not open the county's own tax pages.

What happens to Stafford County property tax when the house sells?

Unpaid property tax is settled from the sale proceeds, because the county's tax lien ranks ahead of other liens until the treasurer is paid. Penalty and interest count as part of the tax owed.

The Commissioner of the Revenue assesses property, and the Treasurer collects the tax. Both are elected county officers. Call them for your parcel's current balance and deadlines.

Is Stafford County part of Northern Virginia?

Yes. Stafford County is in the Washington metropolitan area and is generally counted in Northern Virginia, about 25 miles south of Washington, D.C. by Wikipedia's account.

Unpaid taxes stay as a lien on the house until paid. Virginia law also lets heirs who claim ownership by will or intestacy ask the treasurer to pause a tax sale, and installment plans can run up to 72 months.

Yes. The tax is paid from the proceeds at closing, and the treasurer releases the lien afterward. If the debt is larger than the sale price, you will need to talk to the treasurer and your closing agent first.

Stafford covers 280 square miles, with 269 of them land. It borders Prince William, Fauquier, Culpeper, Caroline, King George and Spotsylvania counties, the City of Fredericksburg, and Charles County, Maryland, across the Potomac.

Albemarle County by the numbers

Where is Albemarle County, VA, and what surrounds it?

Albemarle County is in the Virginia Piedmont, covers about 726 square miles, and wraps around the independent city of Charlottesville. It borders eight other counties, more than any other county in the state, and its western edge runs inside Shenandoah National Park (Wikipedia).

The south fork of the Rivanna River forms in the county, and the James River marks its border with Buckingham County. Scottsville is the largest incorporated town. Places that show up in addresses and fire station names include Crozet, North Garden, Earlysville, Stony Point, Ivy, Pantops, Hollymead and Monticello.

Charlottesville is an independent city, and the county seat sits inside it even though the surrounding land is Albemarle County. The county posts assessment data in its GIS-Web viewer, which is the place to confirm that your parcel is in the county before you look up a bill.

How is land in Albemarle County divided between growth areas and rural land?

Albemarle's comprehensive plan directs new development into Development Areas that make up about 5 percent of the county, while the rest is Rural Area meant for agriculture, natural resource protection and some homes. The Board of Supervisors adopted the current plan, AC44, on October 15, 2025 (county comprehensive plan page).

The county's assessment reports also sort property that way: urban residential on county water and sewer, residential up to 20 acres, and rural parcels of 20 to 99.99 acres and 100 acres or more.

What is the history behind Albemarle County?

The county was created in 1744 from Goochland County and named for the second Earl of Albemarle, and its boundaries were settled in 1777 when Fluvanna County was formed. The county seat moved to Charlottesville in 1761, and Thomas Jefferson was born in what is now the county and built Monticello there.

Before European settlement the area was home to the Saponi. Before the Civil War most of the population was enslaved African Americans, and the Battle of Rio Hill was fought in the county during the war.

What drives the Albemarle County economy?

The University of Virginia is the largest name among local employers, and the county reports low unemployment. The 2022 unemployment rate was 2.7 percent against 3.6 percent nationally, and about 65 percent of workers commute into the county.

  • University of Virginia and Sentara Healthcare
  • U.S. Department of Defense and Northrop Grumman
  • County of Albemarle and Albemarle County Public Schools
  • Crutchfield Corporation, Walmart and Piedmont Virginia Community College

Albemarle County Public Schools serves nearly 14,000 students across 25 facilities. The 2020 census counted 112,395 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 118,356.

What did the 2026 Albemarle County reassessment show?

The county's total tax base rose 6.17 percent in the 2026 reassessment, driven by continued appreciation in residential values. Staff review about 20 percent of properties in detail each year, and in 2026 they reviewed more than 16,000 (county news release, January 21, 2026). The first-half bills mailed in May use the 2026 value and the rate adopted in April.

By magisterial district the average change ranged from +3.6% in Rivanna to +9.8% in Samuel Miller, and the Town of Scottsville averaged +4.1%. The county warns that individual neighborhoods change at different rates, so your own notice can differ widely from these averages.

How do you challenge an Albemarle County assessment?

Albemarle has two appeal steps: an administrative review, then a Board of Equalization appeal. The 2026 cycle ran as follows, and the dates move a little each year.

  • Notices mailed January 23, with data online in the county GIS the next day.
  • Administrative Review form due March 2.
  • Board of Equalization application due March 30, or 30 days after an Administrative Review result, whichever is later.
  • First-half bills mailed in May, based on the new value and the rate the Board of Supervisors adopts in April.

The county suggests calling the Assessor's Office at 434-296-5856 before filing anything. Virginia requires real estate to be assessed at 100 percent of fair market value (Va. Code 58.1-3201), so your argument is about value, not the rate.

What is the Albemarle County real estate tax rate?

The county's tax rates page lists a real estate rate of $0.894 per $100 of assessed value for residential, commercial and land (tax rates page). The page we opened does not show a tax year, so confirm the current figure with the Finance Department before you estimate a bill.

As a rough method, divide the assessed value by 100 and multiply by the rate. The county adopts the rate each April, and the first-half bill in May uses it.

The same page lists a 1 percent daily short-term rental tax and a 9 percent transient occupancy tax effective July 1, 2024. Owners who rent a house short term should keep those accounts current before a sale.

What relief programs does Albemarle County offer?

The county offers real estate tax relief for certain elderly and permanently disabled owners, and a land use program that defers tax on qualifying farm and forest land. The figures below come from the county's most recent notices that we could open, so check the current year.

  • Relief, 2024 program year: owner of record at least 65 or certified totally and permanently disabled, combined income no more than $88,800, and net worth no more than $305,000. First-time applicants were due October 31, 2024. Finance can help at 434-296-5852.
  • Land use: the 2026 application window closed January 1, but owners whose notice showed an increase or who held a newly created parcel could apply through February 24 with a $125 non-refundable fee per parcel.

If you sell land in the program, ask the Assessor's Office what happens to the deferral before you close.

What does it cost to transfer a house in Albemarle County?

Virginia charges a state recordation tax of 25 cents per $100 on a deed and a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 (Va. Code 58.1-801, 58.1-802). The recordation tax applies to the greater of the price or the most recent assessment.

The grantor's tax is imposed on the seller as grantor. Local recordation and other fees are set separately, so ask the title company for a full statement.

How does selling with tax due work in Albemarle County?

A seller with an unpaid Albemarle tax bill can sell, and the title company pays the balance from proceeds. Ask for a payoff that includes penalty and interest, and check that the second-half bill is covered if closing falls near the due date.

The Finance Department can be reached at 434-296-5852 and the Assessor's Office at 434-296-5856. This page is general information, and a Virginia attorney can advise on your title.

More questions about Albemarle County, VA Property Tax Guide

Is Charlottesville part of Albemarle County?

No. Charlottesville is an independent city entirely surrounded by Albemarle County, and Albemarle's county seat is located there. Each government bills its own property tax.

What was the 2026 Albemarle County reassessment?

The county's total tax base rose 6.17 percent, with residential property up 5.4 to 8.1 percent depending on type. Notices were mailed on January 23, 2026.

How do I appeal my Albemarle County assessment?

File the Administrative Review form by March 2 in the 2026 cycle, then apply to the Board of Equalization by March 30 or 30 days after the review result, whichever is later. Call the Assessor at 434-296-5856 first.

What is the Albemarle County real estate tax rate?

Who qualifies for Albemarle County elderly tax relief?

In the 2024 program year, owners had to be 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, with income of no more than $88,800 and net worth of no more than $305,000. Check the county for current limits.

Arlington County by the numbers

What kind of county is Arlington, Virginia?

Arlington is a small, fully urban county directly across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C. It covers about 26 square miles, which makes it the smallest self-governing county in the country by area.

It borders Fairfax County, the City of Falls Church and the City of Alexandria. There are no separate towns inside it, and the Court House neighborhood is the seat of government. The 2020 census counted 238,643 residents.

The county was part of Fairfax County from 1742 and was known as Alexandria County from 1801. It returned to Virginia on March 13, 1847, after the District of Columbia gave back its Virginia portion, and it took the name Arlington in 1920. A five-member county board that appoints a county manager has run it since 1930.

Which Arlington neighborhoods do owners and buyers talk about?

The areas most often named are Rosslyn, Clarendon, Ballston, Pentagon City and Court House. Four Metro lines (Orange, Blue, Silver and Yellow) serve the county, and Interstates 395 and 66 cross it.

Arlington assesses every parcel as of January 1 each year, so the number on your notice is the starting point for any question about your tax, wherever in the county the house sits.

What drives the Arlington economy?

The federal government is the county's largest employer, and the Pentagon, which houses the Department of Defense headquarters, is inside the county. Private employers named on the county's profile include Amazon, Deloitte, Accenture and Booz Allen Hamilton.

Reagan National Airport, which opened in 1941, also lies in Arlington. The airport was built on former Abingdon Plantation land. Arlington's history also includes the 1959 desegregation of Stratford Junior High School, a reminder that the county's older neighborhoods have a long documented past.

When are Arlington County real estate taxes due?

Arlington bills real estate tax in two equal installments. The first is due June 15 and the second is due October 5.

If a due date lands on a weekend or holiday, a payment made the next business day avoids the late penalty. The county page says taxpayers are responsible for knowing the due dates under the Code of Virginia, so a missing bill does not excuse a late payment.

  • If a mortgage company pays through escrow, you get no bill unless the Treasurer's Office does not receive the payment.
  • If you sold and the buyer took over the bill, send the bill back to the Treasurer's Office with what you know about the new owner.
  • Address changes for billing go in writing to the Department of Real Estate Assessments.

What is the Arlington real estate tax rate?

For calendar year 2025 the rate was $1.033 per $100 of assessed value. Commercial property, such as office buildings and hotels, pays an extra $0.125 per $100.

The County Board adopts the rate each April. The county's own example shows a $400,000 assessment producing a $4,132 annual tax at that rate. A later year's rate may differ, so use the figure on your current bill.

How does Arlington assess your house?

Assessments take effect as of January 1 each year and are mailed and posted online each January. Arlington defines fair market value as the price a property would sell for under normal conditions.

The county uses a 12-month sales period that starts 16 months before the effective date. For 2026 that period ran from September 1, 2024 through August 31, 2025. A single sale has only a diluted effect on assessments, since the county studies all sales in a neighborhood.

How do you appeal an Arlington assessment?

There are four steps, and you can skip some of them. Each has its own deadline.

  • Talk to a neighborhood appraiser at 703-228-3920 or assessments@arlingtonva.us.
  • File a Department Review Request. The appeals page gives March 1 and the county FAQ gives March 2, so use the date printed on your notice.
  • File with the Board of Equalization by April 15. It has seven county residents appointed annually and works independently of the assessment office.
  • Sue in Circuit Court at 1425 North Courthouse Road, phone 703-228-7010, which is the final option.

If you have no determination letter by April 1, the county suggests filing the Board of Equalization appeal anyway to keep that door open. You may go straight to the board without a department review. A review can lower the value, confirm it or raise it.

In a department review an appraiser contacts you to schedule an inspection, usually inside and outside the house with a second appraiser present. The appraiser writes a recommendation, a supervisor reviews it and the Director of Real Estate Assessments makes the final call, with written notice by mail or email. You can withdraw or refuse the inspection, though then the review runs on the information the county already has. If someone files for you, the county requires a signed letter of authorization from the owner.

Is there property tax relief in Arlington?

Yes. The Real Estate Tax Relief Program offers an exemption or deferral to homeowners 65 and older and to those who are totally and permanently disabled. The filing deadline given is November 15.

The county listed 2025 limits of annual income up to $105,937 and assets, not counting the home, up to $499,709 for an exemption or $674,606 for a deferral. There is also an exemption for a veteran with a 100 percent service-connected, permanent and total disability, and a surviving spouse may qualify. Limits change, so confirm them with the county before filing.

What happens to the tax bill when you sell in Arlington?

Settle who pays at closing. The Treasurer's Office says responsibility for the taxes should be settled during the sale settlement and that your settlement attorney can answer who pays.

Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 gives the tax a lien on the real estate that ranks ahead of other liens until it is paid, and the seller's share is prorated by contract. State law also caps a locality's late penalty at 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest at 10 percent a year. We did not confirm Arlington's own penalty terms, so ask the Treasurer at 2100 Clarendon Blvd, Suite 201.

On the deed, section 58.1-802 sets a grantor tax of 50 cents per $500, usually paid by the seller, and section 58.1-801 sets the state recordation tax at 25 cents per $100.

When does a cash sale make sense in Arlington?

It can help when a house needs work you do not want to pay for, when tax or a loan is behind, or when you are leaving the area on a short timeline. Arlington's tax bill is billed twice a year, so an unpaid June or October installment can build up quickly on a house that sits empty.

You can compare any offer, ours included, with the county's January 1 value on your notice. We buy as is and give a written cash offer. You can call or text with the address and we will take it from there.

June 15 and October 5. If a date falls on a weekend or holiday, paying the next business day avoids the penalty.

$1.033 per $100 of assessed value, plus $0.125 per $100 for commercial property. The County Board adopts the rate each April.

April 15. Forms must be delivered, postmarked or filed online by midnight that day.

Possibly. The Real Estate Tax Relief Program covers owners 65 and older and those totally and permanently disabled, subject to income and asset limits. The filing deadline is November 15.

Hanover County by the numbers

Where is Hanover County, Virginia, and how big is it?

Hanover County sits about 12 miles north of Richmond and about 90 miles south of Washington, D.C., and it is part of the Greater Richmond Region. The county seat is Hanover, also called Hanover Courthouse, and the only incorporated town inside the county is Ashland.

The Census Bureau lists the county at 474 square miles, with 469 of them land. Its neighbors are Caroline, Goochland, Henrico, King William, Louisa, New Kent and Spotsylvania counties. The Chickahominy River marks the border near Mechanicsville, which is the largest census-designated place.

MeasureFigure

That 82 percent owner share is high. Most Hanover County sellers are individual homeowners, not landlords, and that shapes the kind of sale we see here.

What is the history behind Hanover County?

Hanover County was carved out of the part of New Kent County called St. Peter's Parish and named for the Electorate of Hanover, because King George I was Elector of Hanover at the time. Planters moving west from the Tidewater, where tobacco had worn out the soil, settled much of it.

Patrick Henry was born and raised here, and at Hanover Courthouse in 1763 he argued the Parson's Cause. Henry Clay was born in the county as well. The courthouse appears on the county seal.

The location between Richmond and northern Virginia also made it a battleground. The Seven Days Battles and the 1864 Battle of Cold Harbor were fought on Hanover ground. Later arrivals changed the county in other ways: the Barksdale Theatre opened at Hanover Tavern in 1953, and Kings Dominion opened in Doswell in 1975.

Why does this matter to a seller? Older farmhouses and village homes near Ashland and Hanover Courthouse sit alongside postwar subdivisions around Mechanicsville, so the age and condition of a Hanover County house can vary widely from one road to the next.

Which roads, communities and employers shape Hanover County?

Interstate 95 and Interstate 295 cross the county, and many drivers also use these routes:

  • U.S. 1, U.S. 33, U.S. 301 and U.S. 360
  • State Routes 2, 30, 54, 156 and 326

Communities named by the county's Wikipedia entry include Ashland, Mechanicsville, Hanover, Atlee, Beaverdam, Doswell, Elmont, Montpelier, Old Church, Rockville and Studley, plus the historic Black community of Brown Grove. Ashland is the home of Randolph-Macon College.

An older county employer list reproduced on Wikipedia puts Hanover County government and schools, Bon Secours and Kings Dominion in the 1,000 or more employee range. Tyson Farms, SuperValu and Randolph-Macon College were in the 500 to 999 range. Walmart, Owens and Minor, Kroger, Food Lion and Publix were among the 250 to 499 group. Treat these as a past snapshot and not a current count.

The same source says Bass Pro Shops, FedEx Ground and The Vitamin Shoppe have located in the county. For a seller, the practical point is the mix: retail, distribution, health care and a college give Hanover County a steady base of local jobs, with many residents also commuting toward Richmond.

Which schools serve Hanover County homes?

Hanover County Public Schools runs fifteen elementary schools, four middle schools, four high schools, one alternative school and one technology school. The four high schools are Atlee, Hanover, Mechanicsville and Patrick Henry.

Buyers often ask which high school a house feeds, so a seller should have the address ready for the school division's attendance lookup. We do not publish attendance zones here because we have not confirmed them on an official page.

Which Hanover County offices handle real estate tax?

Hanover County has an elected Commissioner of the Revenue and an elected Treasurer, along with a Clerk of the Circuit Court. In Virginia, the assessing office sets the value and the Treasurer sends and collects the bill, while the Clerk records the deed when the house sells.

We could not open the county's own tax pages for this guide, so we are not stating Hanover County's current tax rate, installment due dates or appeal deadline. Please call the Treasurer and the assessing office to confirm them before you rely on any date.

Ask these questions on the call:

  • What is the current balance on my parcel, and does it include penalty or interest?
  • When is the next installment due, and what is the last day to pay without penalty?
  • What is the deadline to appeal this year's assessment?
  • Can the bill be reissued to the buyer if the house sells after a bill has been mailed?

How does a Virginia assessment appeal work for a Hanover County owner?

Under Virginia law, a local board of equalization starts from the presumption that the assessor's value is correct, so the owner has the burden of proof. To win, the owner must show by a preponderance of the evidence that the home is valued above fair market value, or that the assessment is not uniform and was not set under accepted appraisal practice.

For a residential property with fewer than four units, the assessing officer must give written notice and, on written request, provide the assessment records within 15 days. Evidence is limited as well. The board may consider sales through December 31 before the assessment's effective date, as long as they reach the board by the locality's deadline, and studies published after that December 31 are not considered.

In practice, a Hanover County owner builds a file of recent comparable sales, photos of defects and any factual errors, such as the wrong square footage. The statute treats mistakes of fact, including computation errors, as a departure from accepted practice. You can read the rule in Virginia Code 58.1-3379.

What happens to Hanover County real estate tax when a house is sold?

When a Virginia house changes hands after a tax bill has been mailed, the Treasurer may cancel the bill sent to the old owner and reissue it to the new owner. If the new owner pays within two weeks of the reissued notice, no penalty may be charged for that assessment.

State law caps late penalties on real estate at 10 percent of the tax past due, and interest may not exceed 10 percent a year for the first year, with a different ceiling in later years. A locality may also recover collection fees it has contracted for, up to 20 percent of the delinquent amount. The exact Hanover County figures are set by county ordinance, so confirm them with the Treasurer.

The Commonwealth also taxes the deed itself. The grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value, and the seller pays it unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. The clerk must certify payment before the deed can be recorded, and the money is split between the state and the locality. See Virginia Code 58.1-802.

What can a Hanover County seller do if the tax bill is behind?

A seller with unpaid tax has three realistic paths: pay the balance from sale proceeds at closing, ask the Treasurer about extension or payment options, or sell to a buyer who will take the house as it stands. A locality may grant extensions of up to 90 days by resolution when good cause exists, and a taxpayer who misses a deadline because of a death or a documented medical impairment is presumed to be without fault if payment comes within 30 days.

An assessment under administrative appeal also gets breathing room. If the appeal is filed within 90 days of the assessment, the bill is not treated as delinquent while the appeal is pending, and for 30 days after the final decision.

If the house is inherited, vacant or needs work, Cash Home Buyers can look at it as is and explain how the tax balance would be handled at closing. A written cash offer carries no obligation, and you can compare it with other options at your own pace.

The county Treasurer sends and collects the bill, and the Commissioner of the Revenue and the assessing office handle values. Call both offices to confirm the current installment dates, since we could not verify them on an official page.

What is the Hanover County property tax appeal deadline?

The county sets its own deadline, and we have not confirmed it, so call the assessing office before you plan. Virginia law places the burden on the owner to show the value is too high or not uniform.

Can penalties on Hanover County property tax be waived?

Virginia law bars penalty and interest when the failure was not the taxpayer's fault, including certain postal errors, and presumes no fault after a death or medical impairment when payment follows within 30 days. The Treasurer decides fault for late payments.

Who pays the Virginia deed tax when selling a house in Hanover County?

The seller, as grantor, pays the state grantor tax of 50 cents per $500 unless the contract assigns some of it to the buyer. The Clerk of the Circuit Court collects it at recording.

Is Hanover County mostly owner-occupied?

Yes. The 2020 census shows 82.0 percent of occupied housing units owner-occupied and 18.0 percent rented, out of 43,184 housing units.

Where is Caroline County, Virginia, and what kind of county is it?

Caroline County sits in eastern Virginia with the Rappahannock River along its northern edge. It is about 30 miles north of Richmond and 32 miles south of Fredericksburg, which puts it between two job centers.

The county covers 537 square miles and had 30,887 residents in the 2020 census. That is roughly double its population fifty years earlier, so many of the homes here are fairly recent additions to an older farming landscape. Bowling Green is the county seat and the largest town, and Port Royal is the only other incorporated town.

The county was established in 1727 and named for Queen Caroline of Ansbach. Tobacco and mixed farming shaped its early history, and later the county became known for thoroughbred horse farms. Secretariat, the 1973 Triple Crown winner, was born at The Meadow here.

What does the local economy mean for a house in Caroline County?

Most of the county economy is a mix of agriculture, distribution, military training and event business, and plenty of residents drive out of the county to work. A buyer or investor looking at a Caroline County house is often thinking about the commute along Interstate 95 as much as the lot itself.

  • Fort A.P. Hill, a military training complex of about 77,000 acres, was established in 1941.
  • The State Fair of Virginia moved to Meadow Event Park in 2009.
  • McKesson built a 340,000 square foot distribution center in the county.
  • M.C. Dean and Remuda Programs are other businesses named in the county's profile.

Caroline County Public Schools reported 490 employees in the 2020 to 2021 school year, including 209 teachers, so the school system is also a steady local employer.

Which highways and rail lines serve Caroline County?

Interstate 95 crosses the county, with exits 104 and 110, and U.S. Routes 1, 17 and 301 also run through it. State Routes 2, 30 and 207 fill in the local network.

Amtrak and CSX freight trains use the Richmond, Fredericksburg and Potomac rail corridor, which passes through Milford. For a seller, access to I-95 is usually the first thing a buyer asks about, and houses near an exit tend to be easier to describe than houses at the end of a long rural road.

When are Caroline County real estate taxes due?

Real estate tax in Caroline County is due on June 5 and December 5. The county's own Dates to Remember page says a 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest are added on June 6 and December 6 for real estate, personal property and business personal property.

ItemWhat the county lists
First installmentJune 5

Penalty and interest10 percent each, added the next day
Water billsDue 15 days from the billing date
