Virginia law sets the outer limits. Under Code of Virginia 58.1-3916, a locality may charge interest of up to 10 percent a year and a penalty of up to 10 percent of the past-due property tax. The same section lets a locality waive both when the failure was not the taxpayer's fault, or when a payment was mailed on time with proof of mailing and arrived within five days of the deadline.

Who do you call at the Caroline County Treasurer and Commissioner of the Revenue?

The Treasurer collects the tax and the Commissioner of the Revenue handles assessment questions. They are separate offices with separate contacts.

  • Treasurer: 212 N Main Street, Bowling Green, VA 22427. Mail goes to P.O. Box 431. Phone 804-633-5291, open Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Real estate questions at the Commissioner's office: 804-633-9834 or realestate@co.caroline.va.us.
  • General county mail: P.O. Box 447, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

The Treasurer accepts payment online, by phone through ACI, by mail, in person, or by monthly automatic withdrawal. There is a drop box in front of the County Administration Building for after-hours payments. The county says it guarantees only payments made through its own website and Official Payments, so a payment sent through a personal bank bill-pay service is at the taxpayer's risk.

How do you check or appeal a Caroline County assessment?

Start with the county's online assessment search and the Commissioner's real estate office, then use the Board of Equalization if you disagree. The county publishes a Real Estate Assessment Information tool at caroline.civ.quest, and a Tax Map page that shows parcels.

The county describes the appeal path this way. Owners with concerns about a reassessment first go to hearings with the Board of Assessors. A Board of Equalization is then set up to review complaints. It is a six member citizen panel, nominated by the Board of Supervisors and approved by a Circuit Court judge in each general reassessment year, and its members must complete training from the Virginia Department of Taxation. After the Board finishes, the county says the only option left is a petition to the Circuit Court under Section 58.1-3984 of the Code of Virginia.

The county pages we opened do not state a filing deadline for real estate appeals, so ask the Commissioner's office for the dates in any reassessment year before you rely on one.

State law helps the owner prepare. Under 58.1-3379, the assessor's value is presumed correct, and the owner must show it is above fair market value, applied unevenly, or not made under accepted appraisal practice. For a residential property with fewer than four units, the assessing officer must hand over the assessment records within 15 days of a written request.

What local rules matter when selling a house in Caroline County?

The main ones are building permits, land use programs, utilities and the recordation cost at closing. Each has its own office, so confirm them early.

A certificate of occupancy is issued after satisfactory completion, and the Building Inspections office can be reached at 804-633-4303. Unpermitted work is worth sorting out before listing.
  • Land use: the Commissioner of the Revenue runs the land preservation program and rechecks each enrolled property every year. The county page does not list acreage or rollback rules, so ask that office if your parcel is enrolled.
  • Utilities: the county names the Carmel Church Ladysmith, Milford, Port Royal and Townfield water systems. Public Utilities is at 804-633-4390.
  • Elderly and disabled relief: questions go to the real estate office at 804-633-9834.

At closing, Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value, under 58.1-802. The statute puts it on the seller, though buyer and seller may agree otherwise.

What do sellers in Caroline County usually face with unpaid tax?

Sellers with unpaid tax usually face stacked penalty and interest and a larger payoff at closing. Because the county adds 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest the day after each due date, a missed December 5 bill grows right away.

Ask the Treasurer for the balance on the day you expect to close, and ask the closing agent to confirm it. If the house needs work that a retail buyer would not accept, a cash buyer who purchases as is can save the repair and showing time, and the unpaid balance can be paid from proceeds at closing.

June 5 and December 5. The county adds a 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest on June 6 and December 6 for real estate and personal property.

At 212 N Main Street in Bowling Green, open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The phone number is 804-633-5291, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 431, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

How do I appeal a Caroline County real estate assessment?

Talk to the Commissioner of the Revenue's real estate office first, then go to the Board of Equalization if you still disagree. After that, the county says the only remaining step is a Circuit Court petition under Section 58.1-3984 of the Code of Virginia.

Can I sell a Caroline County house if I owe back taxes?

Yes, in most cases the balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a current payoff figure and have your closing agent confirm it.

Who pays the Virginia grantor tax when a Caroline County house sells?

The statute puts the 50 cents per $500 grantor tax on the seller, but buyer and seller may agree that the buyer pays some or all of it.

Augusta County by the numbers

Where is Augusta County, Virginia, and how big is it?

Augusta County is in the Shenandoah Valley on the western side of Virginia, and it is one of the largest counties in the state. Its total area is 971 square miles, which Wikipedia lists as second in Virginia by total area and third by land area.

The county completely surrounds the independent cities of Staunton and Waynesboro, and those cities are not part of it. That detail matters for a seller. A house with a Staunton or Waynesboro mailing address may be taxed by the city, while a house just outside the line is taxed by Augusta County.

Most residents live in unincorporated communities. The 2010 census figures listed on Wikipedia show Stuarts Draft as the largest at 9,235, followed by Fishersville at 7,462 and Verona at 4,239. Weyers Cave, Crimora and Churchville are smaller.

Two towns sit inside the county. Craigsville had 923 residents in 2010. Grottoes is mostly in Rockingham County, and only seven of its residents live on the Augusta side.

What is Augusta County's history?

The county was formed in 1738 from Orange County and named for Princess Augusta of Saxe-Gotha. County government was organized in 1745 and the present boundaries were reached in 1790.

During the Civil War the area was an important agricultural center, and the Battle of Piedmont was fought here on June 5, 1864.

Who are the major employers in Augusta County?

According to the county's 2023 financial report, four employers each have more than 1,000 workers: Augusta County Public Schools, Augusta Medical Center, Hershey and McKee Foods.

A seller whose job or a relative's care moves them out of the area can sell without waiting on a long financing process. We buy houses as they are.

When are Augusta County real estate taxes due?

Taxes are due in equal installments on June 5 and December 5. If a date falls on a weekend, the due date moves to the following Monday, and you may pay the full annual amount in June.

In 2024 the county extended the first-half date to June 21. The county's real estate page also says the 2024 rate is $0.52 per $100 of assessed value, set by the Board of Supervisors, and that real estate is assessed as of January 1 by the Real Estate Assessor's Office. Bills can be viewed and paid on the county's e-Treasurer site. We did not confirm the current year's rate, so check your bill.

The county states a 10 percent late payment penalty on the unpaid balance, plus interest at 10 percent a year on what remains unpaid. The state's share of personal property tax is excluded from the interest.

The county also tells taxpayers that they are responsible for knowing due dates. If no bill arrives, contact the taxing office before the due date to arrange payment.

Some reasons never waive the charge. These include not knowing the due date, not getting a bill, a bill mailed to the wrong address, an incorrect bill and wrong information from county staff. The charge may be waived in narrower cases.

  • The Commissioner of Revenue abates the tax or certifies a clerical error by that office.
  • The late payment was caused solely by the Treasurer or the Commissioner of Revenue.

A taxpayer who cannot pay in full may arrange a payment plan with the Treasurer's Office at (540) 245-5660 or treasurer@co.augusta.va.us. The plan does not remove the penalty and interest keeps running.

How did the 2024 reassessment change values in Augusta County?

The county reassesses on a five-year cycle, and the 2024 reassessment began in September 2022 with notices mailed in February 2024. The county hired Wampler-Eanes Appraisal Group and divided the county into about 96 neighborhoods.

Its published analysis of 2023 residential sales found 680 sales with a median increase of 58.3 percent over the old assessment and an average of 60.9 percent. The highest median increases were in Beverly Manor at 69.5 percent and North River at 68.8 percent. The lowest were in Craigsville at 33.7 percent, based on only three sales, and Wayne at 50.9 percent.

The county's document also explains why it reassesses: the state's sales ratio study flags a locality whose assessments fall below 70 percent of fair market value in a general reassessment year. Augusta's ratios were 89.75 percent in 2019, 83.73 percent in 2020 and 71.7 percent in 2021. Fieldwork included visits to accessible properties to verify records and update property cards and photos.

That context helps a seller. Many owners saw their assessed value rise sharply in 2024, and your new value is a county estimate, not a sale price.

How do you appeal an Augusta County assessment?

The county's reassessment materials describe three steps: an informal hearing with the assessor, the Board of Equalization, then Circuit Court. Informal appeals could be made by Zoom, phone, email, mail or in person.

  • Common reasons given: value that seems too high or too low, market value disparities, changes in condition, comparable sales and clerical errors.
  • The county material did not list deadlines, so use the dates on your notice.

Under Virginia Code section 58.1-3381 the board can increase, decrease or affirm an assessment, and an owner must be notified before an increase. In court, section 58.1-3984 treats the assessor's value as correct and puts the burden on the owner to rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence.

What happens to unpaid tax when you sell in Augusta County?

The unpaid tax stays with the property. Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 gives real estate a tax lien that ranks ahead of other liens until paid, and sale proceeds are applied to the tax. How the current year's tax is split between buyer and seller is set by the contract.

On the deed, the grantor tax under section 58.1-802 is 50 cents for each $500 and is paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise. The state recordation tax under section 58.1-801 is 25 cents per $100.

State law sets the outer limits on late charges. Section 58.1-3916 caps a locality's penalty at 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest at 10 percent a year, which matches the figures Augusta County publishes. No. They are independent cities that Augusta County surrounds. A house inside either city is generally handled by the city, so check which office bills you.

Where is Roanoke County, VA, and which governments sit inside it?

Roanoke County is in southwest Virginia, in the Roanoke Valley, and it surrounds two independent cities: Roanoke and Salem. Those cities are inside the county's boundaries but are not part of it, and the town of Vinton is the only incorporated town within the county itself.

The county was created on March 30, 1838 from the southern part of Botetourt County. Salem is the county seat, and the courthouse remained there when Salem became an independent city in 1968, but the county's administrative offices were moved to the Cave Spring area. If you need an appointment or a form, check which building you are headed to.

The county covers about 251 square miles. The 2020 census counted 96,929 people, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 97,150. Most residents live in the suburbs around Roanoke and Salem, while large areas to the north, west and south are rural and mountainous.

Why does a Roanoke mailing address not always mean you pay Roanoke County tax?

Many addresses in the county use a Roanoke or Salem mailing address even though the parcel is inside Roanoke County. Wikipedia notes that many of the county's communities have mailing addresses in the two cities.

This matters for your tax bill because the county, the city of Roanoke, the city of Salem and the town of Vinton are different governments with different rates and offices. Before you try to appeal an assessment, pay a bill or ask for a payoff figure, confirm which locality actually bills your parcel. What does the county look like for a seller?

Roanoke County skews older and owner-occupied. In the 2020 census the median age was 44.5, and 22.1 percent of residents were 65 or older. The county had 39,777 households and 42,147 housing units, of which 5.6 percent were vacant. Of the occupied units, 75.5 percent were owner-occupied and 24.5 percent were rented.

The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.3 percent, and the rental vacancy rate was 7.7 percent. In plain language, a large majority of local housing is owned by the people who live in it, and rentals are a smaller part of the picture.

With that much owner-occupied housing, an inherited family house or a downsizing sale is a common reason to sell.

Education options in the county include five public high schools: Cave Spring, Glenvar, Hidden Valley, Northside and William Byrd. Hollins University is in northern Roanoke County, and Roanoke College is in Salem.

How do roads and terrain affect property in Roanoke County?

Interstate 81 and Interstate 581 cross the county, along with US 11, US 220, US 221 and US 460 and several state routes. The Blue Ridge Parkway and a part of the Jefferson National Forest are also inside its boundaries.

Much of the county is rural and mountainous, so some parcels have private roads, wells or septic systems. Virginia's seller disclosure statement tells buyers that the owner makes no statement about wastewater systems, lot lines, easements and special flood hazard areas, and urges them to investigate. Having a recent survey, a septic pumping record and a driveway maintenance agreement ready can save a deal.

If your parcel is large, ask the county's real estate valuation office whether any special land-use program applies. A change in how land is used can trigger additional taxes, and Virginia's disclosure form that takes effect on January 1, 2027 adds a line about roll-back taxes for land taxed on its use.

How can a Roanoke County owner appeal a real estate assessment?

An owner who disagrees with an assessment can ask the county's real estate valuation office for an informal review, and Virginia law also provides a Board of Equalization hearing. The county site listing summarized above gives a phone number for informal review, so confirm it with the office.

At the Board of Equalization, Virginia law places the burden on the taxpayer. The assessor's value is presumed correct, and you have to show by a preponderance of the evidence that the property is valued above its fair market value, or that the assessment is not uniform or was not set under accepted appraisal practice. The board can raise as well as lower assessments to keep the tax burden even.

  • Market sales that occurred through December 31 before the assessment's effective date can be considered, if you submit them by the locality's deadline.
  • Studies published after that December 31 cannot be considered.
  • For a residential property with fewer than four units, you can ask in writing for the assessor's records, and the assessor must provide them within 15 days.

The statute is Virginia Code 58.1-3379. Because deadlines vary by locality and by year, ask the county for this year's cutoff date before you gather evidence.

What is the difference between an appeal and a correction request?

A correction request goes to the commissioner of the revenue or equivalent officer, while an appeal to the board asks for a new valuation. Under Virginia Code 58.1-3980, the correction process applies to real estate only when the error was made by the assessing office itself, or was a factual error made by others during a general reassessment.

The deadline is the later of three years from the last day of the tax year in question or one year from the date of the assessment. An example would be a wrong square footage on your record, a house listed with a finished basement that does not exist, or a parcel counted twice. That kind of mistake can be fixed without arguing about market value.

What happens to a tax balance when a Roanoke County house is sold?

Real estate tax is a lien that comes ahead of all other liens, and it stays on the property until the tax authority is actually paid. The closing agent must apply the sale proceeds to unpaid taxes, including penalties and interest, and the treasurer releases the lien after payment.

Virginia law also says the seller's tax liability is prorated by contract, so the purchase agreement should state who owes what for the current year. If you sell only part of a tract, the proceeds go toward taxes on the whole tract in proportion to the price, and the assessing office may ask for an appraisal if the price looks low. The text is in Virginia Code 58.1-3340.

The state grantor's tax is a separate item. It is 50 cents for each $500 of the price, paid by the seller unless the contract says otherwise, and split between the state and the locality. See Virginia Code 58.1-802.

For a house with unpaid taxes, a cash sale can keep the closing simple. The title company deducts the tax balance from the proceeds and sends it to the treasurer, and you receive what remains. No. Salem is an independent city that sits inside the county's boundaries. It is the county seat, but the county's administrative offices are in the Cave Spring area.

The taxpayer does. Under Virginia Code 58.1-3379 the assessor's value is presumed correct, and you must show it is above fair market value or not uniform.

Can I fix a factual error on my assessment after the deadline for an appeal?

Sometimes. A correction request to the assessing officer can be filed within three years of the end of the tax year or one year from the assessment, whichever is later, but only for errors made by the assessing office or in a general reassessment.

Does the buyer or seller pay the real estate tax lien at closing?

The closing agent pays unpaid tax from the sale proceeds, so in practice the seller's share comes out of the seller's money. The contract prorates the current year between buyer and seller.

It is 50 cents per $500 of the price, paid by the seller unless the buyer agrees to pay it, and the clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

Where is Giles County, Virginia, and how is it laid out?

Giles County sits in southwestern Virginia on the West Virginia state line, and its county seat is Pearisburg. It covers 360 square miles, of which 356 are land, and it is part of the Blacksburg-Christiansburg metropolitan area.

Neighbors include Summers, Monroe and Mercer counties in West Virginia, plus Craig, Montgomery, Pulaski and Bland counties in Virginia. Part of the Jefferson National Forest lies inside the county, and Mountain Lake, one of only two natural freshwater lakes in Virginia, drains through Little Stony Creek and over The Cascades to the New River.

Four incorporated towns remain: Narrows, Pearisburg, Pembroke and Rich Creek. Glen Lyn dissolved as a town in 2024 and is now an unincorporated community. How did Giles County get its name and shape?

The General Assembly formed Giles County in 1806 from parts of Montgomery, Monroe, Wythe and Tazewell counties. It is named for William Branch Giles, a Virginia lawyer who served in Congress and later as governor.

Because the county was cut from several older ones, old deeds can cite a parent county or a different road name. If a seller inherited land with a very old legal description, the Giles County Circuit Court clerk's land records are where the chain of title is kept.

The county also has an unusual geologic footnote. A magnitude 5.9 earthquake centered here on May 31, 1897 was among the strongest in Virginia, damaged chimneys near the epicenter and derailed a train. Older masonry chimneys are still worth a look during an inspection of an old house.

What do people in Giles County do for work, and how does that touch housing?

Giles County is entirely rural by census definition, and many households are small. In 2020, 29.4% of households were one person, and 22.2% of residents were 65 or older.

We are not listing individual employers because we did not open an official source naming them. What the housing numbers show is a county with slow population movement: 16,787 residents in 2020 against 17,286 in 2010, and an estimated 16,564 in 2025.

For a seller, a county with fewer buyers per listing often means a house stays on the market longer, especially if it needs work or sits on a back road. That is the situation where owners ask about selling to a cash buyer instead of preparing a house for the open market.

Which roads and rail lines serve Giles County?

U.S. 460 (Virginia Avenue in Pearisburg) and U.S. 219 (Federal Street) are the main federal routes. State Routes 42, 61 and 100 also cross the county, and a Norfolk Southern rail line runs through it.

  • U.S. 460 is Virginia Avenue where it passes through Pearisburg.
  • U.S. 219 is Federal Street.
  • State Route 61, the Wolf Creek Highway, serves the Narrows area.
  • State Route 100 runs through the county, and State Route 42 is split into two disconnected pieces.

Road access matters for sale price and for how fast a buyer can get an inspector or a contractor out to the house, so mention a private lane or a gravel road when you describe the property.

Which schools and towns will buyers ask about?

Giles County Public Schools operates Eastern Elementary/Middle School in Pembroke, Macy McClaugherty Elementary/Middle School in Pearisburg, Narrows Elementary/Middle School and two high schools, Giles High School and Narrows High School. The Giles County Technology Center is in Pearisburg.

Which attendance zone a house falls in depends on its address, so confirm with the school division rather than a listing description.

Who bills and who assesses real estate tax in Giles County?

Two elected constitutional offices handle it. The Commissioner of the Revenue keeps the assessment records and takes appeals, and the Treasurer collects the bills.

The county's online real estate data portal states that it shows 2026 reassessment values and ownership as of January 1, 2026. It also says value changes made during the year will not reflect on current billing, because billing is based on January 1, 2026. That means a new roof or an addition finished after that date generally does not change this year's bill.

The portal tells visitors to call the Commissioner of the Revenue's office at (540) 921-3321 with questions, and says the office's records are the authoritative source when researching real estate.

  • Check the parcel number, acreage and building description on the portal before you list or sell.
  • Ask the Commissioner about any land use program or tax relief application that may be on the property.
  • Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure that includes penalty and interest.

When are Giles County real estate taxes due?

Treat any date you read on a third-party site as a guess until the Treasurer confirms it, and ask whether a reassessment year changed the schedule.

How do you challenge a Giles County assessment?

Start with the Commissioner of the Revenue, who made the assessment. Virginia's Code gives anyone assessed by a commissioner of the revenue three years from the end of the tax year, or one year from the date of assessment, whichever is later, to ask for a correction, and that statute applies to real estate when the error was made by the commissioner or was a factual error from a general reassessment.

Virginia also provides for boards of equalization after a general reassessment, and the circuit court is the next level in most localities. We did not find a Giles County page stating the current board filing deadline, so ask the Commissioner's office when the 2026 notices went out and what the cutoff is.

What happens to unpaid tax when a Giles County house sells?

Under Virginia law the tax lien on real estate comes ahead of every other lien and stays until the taxing authority is actually paid. The person who buys at a sale, or the trustee in a foreclosure, must see that sale proceeds go to the taxes assessed on the property, and the word taxes in that statute includes penalties and interest.

On a normal closing the settlement agent asks the Treasurer for a payoff and pays it from the seller's proceeds. The Code also says the seller's liability for taxes is prorated by contract, so the sales contract should state who covers which months.

  1. Get the parcel number from the portal.
  2. Ask the Treasurer for the balance, including penalty and interest.
  3. Give that figure to the title company.
  4. Confirm the lien is released after closing.

What do sellers in Giles County usually face?

Typical situations include inherited homes in towns like Narrows and Pearisburg, older houses on larger rural parcels, and homes with deferred repairs. Does a repair I make this year change my Giles County bill?

Generally no for the current bill. The county portal says value changes made during the year do not reflect on current billing, which is based on January 1, 2026.

Virginia's statute allows three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the assessment date, whichever is later. It covers real estate when the commissioner or a reassessment factual error caused the problem.

Frederick County by the numbers

Where is Frederick County, Virginia?

Frederick County is the northernmost county in Virginia, and its seat is the city of Winchester. Winchester is an independent city, so it is not part of the county even though the county surrounds it.

The county covers 416 square miles and had 91,419 residents in the 2020 census, with a Census Bureau estimate of 99,955 for 2025. It borders Clarke, Warren and Shenandoah counties in Virginia and Hardy, Hampshire, Morgan and Berkeley counties in West Virginia. It belongs to the Winchester, VA-WV metropolitan area, which is part of the Washington-Baltimore combined statistical area.

What is the history of Frederick County?

Frederick County was created from Orange County in 1738 and officially organized in 1743. In its first form it covered parts of what became four Virginia counties and five West Virginia counties.

George Washington made his headquarters in Winchester in 1754 as commander of the Virginia regiment, and his first elected office was a seat in the House of Burgesses representing Frederick County in 1758. During the Civil War control of Winchester shifted between Confederate and Union armies about once every three weeks, and battles were fought in the county at Kernstown, Winchester and Cedar Creek.

Cedar Creek and Belle Grove National Historical Park lies partly in the county, as does part of the George Washington National Forest.

West Virginia's first constitution allowed Frederick County to join the new state if a local election approved. Unlike neighboring Berkeley and Jefferson counties, Frederick stayed in Virginia, since the Confederate army occupied it and no vote was held.

Which towns and neighborhoods make up Frederick County?

Frederick County has two incorporated towns, Middletown and Stephens City, which is the largest. Four census-designated places are listed: Brucetown, Gore, Lake Holiday and Shawneeland.

  • Many of the county's addresses are in unincorporated places such as Kernstown, Clear Brook, Gainesboro, Round Hill, Jordan Springs, Lake Frederick and Mountain Falls.
  • The county article counts 60.6 percent of residents as urban and 39.4 percent as rural in 2020.
  • Wikipedia puts the median age at 40.9 and counts 34,073 households.

Because the city of Winchester is separate from the county, check which jurisdiction sends the tax bill before you call an office.

What roads and transit serve Frederick County?

Interstate 81 and Interstate 66 are the main highways, joined by US 11, 17, 48, 50, 340 and 522 and state routes 7, 37, 55, 127, 259 and 277.

Wikipedia names Winchester Transit as the local bus provider, with weekday service for the city of Winchester.

Which schools and colleges serve Frederick County?

Frederick County Public Schools runs the county's schools, including James Wood High School, Millbrook High School and Sherando High School. The county is also part of the area served by Mountain Vista Governor's School.

Higher education nearby includes Laurel Ridge Community College and Shenandoah University, and the Handley Regional Library serves the area. Wikipedia lists twelve elementary schools, from Apple Pie Ridge and Armel to Redbud Run and Stonewall, and four middle schools: Admiral Richard E. Byrd, Frederick County, James Wood and Robert E. Aylor.

What is the Frederick County real estate tax rate?

Frederick County's tax rate page lists $0.53 per $100 of assessed value for real estate and the same $0.53 for mobile homes. At that rate a house assessed at $350,000 would carry $1,855 a year, or $927.50 per half. That is arithmetic from the posted rate, not a bill.

The page links a real estate calculator you can use with your own assessment.

When are Frederick County real estate taxes due?

Frederick County collects real estate tax in two halves, June 5 and December 5. The Commissioner of the Revenue's calendar says that if the office is closed on a due date, payment is due the next business day.

  • January 1 to April 1: window for elderly and permanently disabled tax relief applications, due April 1.
  • June 5: first half of real estate and personal property tax.
  • November 1: land use applications, with a late filing fee accepted through December 1.
  • December 5: second half.

Tax relief for 100 percent service-connected, totally and permanently disabled veterans, and for surviving spouses of armed forces members killed in action, can be filed at any time. The Treasurer, C. William Orndoff, Jr., also offers an option to pre-pay real estate taxes. The pages reviewed did not state a late penalty, so ask the Treasurer for the current figure.

How do you appeal a Frederick County assessment?

Start by calling the assessor at 540-665-5680. The Commissioner of the Revenue says an owner who thinks a real estate assessment is wrong can appeal when the error was made by the Commissioner or is a factual error by others during a general reassessment.

The county describes these routes.

  1. Assessor hearing at the County Administration Building, 107 North Kent Street, Winchester. Call 540-722-8319 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, to schedule. Hearing dates are published in The Winchester Star and on the website.
  2. Written appeal by email, by letter, or on the Appeal of Assessment form, mailed to Commissioner of the Revenue, Real Property Tax Appeal, PO Box 552, Winchester, VA 22604.
  3. Further appeal to the Board of Equalization and the Frederick County Circuit Court.

The pages reviewed gave no Board of Equalization deadline for this county, so ask the office when the next reassessment cycle opens. Virginia Code 58.1-3984 sets the court timing, and it presumes the assessor's value is right for real property.

What should sellers know about Frederick County land use and tax relief?

The Commissioner's Real Estate Division administers agricultural, horticultural and forest land use assessments as well as tax relief for the elderly and disabled, disabled veterans and surviving spouses of certain persons killed in the line of duty. Its page also links a Tax Sale Information Center.

If your parcel is in land use, ask the office what happens to the deferral on a sale before you set a closing date. The division's page links the program rules.

County websites also post emergency notices. At the time of review the county's pages carried a wildfire update press release dated November 10, so check the home page for current notices if you are showing a rural property.

What happens to Frederick County tax at closing?

Unpaid tax on a Virginia house is a lien that ranks ahead of other liens. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 says it lasts until actual payment, that a sale's proceeds go first to taxes and levies on the real estate, and that penalties and interest count as part of the tax. The seller's share is prorated by contract.

A deed also triggers the grantor's tax under Virginia Code 58.1-802: 50 cents per $500 of consideration, paid by the seller unless the buyer agrees to cover it.

$0.53 per $100 of assessed value, according to the county's tax rate page.

June 5 for the first half and December 5 for the second half. If the office is closed on a due date, the next business day applies.

Call the assessor at 540-665-5680. To schedule a hearing, call 540-722-8319 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays.

Is Winchester part of Frederick County?

No. Winchester is the county seat but is an independent city under Virginia law, and Frederick County surrounds it.

When is the Frederick County tax relief deadline for seniors?

Applications for elderly or permanently disabled relief are accepted from January 1 to April 1.

What is Culpeper County like?

Culpeper County is a Piedmont county in the foothills of the Blue Ridge, about 383 square miles, with the town of Culpeper as its seat. The 2020 census counted 52,552 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 57,666.

Rivers mark two of its edges. The Rappahannock forms the northeast border and the Rapidan the south, while the Hazel River runs east through the middle. Rolling hills slope to the south and east, and the highest point, near the west corner, is 705 feet above sea level.

How did Culpeper County begin?

The county was created in 1749, and its first surveyor was a teenage George Washington. Wikipedia records that the first Culpeper court met that May at the home of Robert Tureman, and Washington was commissioned surveyor in July at age 17.

The name comes from Catherine Culpeper, whose family held the Northern Neck proprietary. In 1833 the upper 267 square miles were split off to form Rappahannock County. Two Civil War engagements took place on Culpeper soil: Cedar Mountain on August 9, 1862, and Brandy Station on June 9, 1863. The Brandy Station Battlefield Park is among the county's protected areas.

The county is also home to Commonwealth Park, site of many equestrian events, and the Culpeper Minutemen, a militia raised here, fought in both the Revolutionary War and the Civil War, per Wikipedia.

Most Culpeper workers leave the county for their jobs. Wikipedia, citing Virginia Employment Commission data, reports a civilian workforce of 24,313, with 30 percent of residents working in the county and 70 percent commuting out, mostly to Fairfax and Fauquier counties.

The same source says in-commuters equal about 45 percent of the local workforce, with the most coming from Orange County.

US 15, US 29, US 211 and US 522 are the main U.S. routes, joined by state routes 3, 229 and 299.

Six counties border it: Fauquier to the north, Stafford to the east, Spotsylvania to the southeast, Orange to the south, Madison to the southwest and Rappahannock to the northwest. Wikipedia says the Blue Ridge, including Old Rag Mountain and the Skyline Drive, is quickly reached up Route 522.

Outside the town, communities named in the county article include Brandy Station (a census-designated place), Stevensburg, Jeffersonton, Rixeyville, Lignum and Richardsville.

The 2020 census counted 18,181 households, a median age of 39.8 and a 5.2 percent vacancy rate across 19,185 housing units. Culpeper County Public Schools covers the whole county. Wikipedia lists Culpeper County High School and Eastern View High School as its high schools, with the Culpeper Technical Education Center also listed. Culpeper Middle and Floyd T. Binns Middle are the middle schools.

The county page says county taxes are due December 5 each year. That is one date, not the two installments used in neighboring counties.

The Treasurer takes payments by mail at Culpeper County Treasurer, PO Box 1447, Culpeper, VA 22701. If you sell in the fall, ask the closing agent to confirm what has been paid and how the December bill will be prorated.

How does Culpeper County reassess property?

Culpeper assesses every two years, on a biennial cycle set by the Board of Supervisors. The assessor's page says the current assessment became effective January 1, 2025 and stays in effect until January 1, 2027, with general reassessments falling in odd years.

The Department of Real Estate Assessments uses one or more of three methods:

  • Sales comparison: recent sales of similar properties, adjusted for size, condition, age, location and amenities.
  • Cost: current materials, labor and depreciation, plus the value of comparable vacant land.
  • Income: industry figures on what a property could earn and what it costs to run.

The same office runs the land use program, which must be revalidated at each general reassessment, and tax relief for elderly and disabled owners, disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses.

How do you appeal a Culpeper County assessment?

The Board of Equalization is the formal route during a reassessment. It is an independent body appointed by the Circuit Court, and it can raise, lower or keep an assessment.

For the 2025 reassessment, the Board of Supervisors set May 1, 2025 for hearings to begin and June 20, 2025 as the last day to apply. The county page says the board is active during the period of the general reassessment, so ask the assessor for the dates tied to the next one.

After that, owners can apply to circuit court. Virginia Code 58.1-3984 lets an aggrieved taxpayer apply within the later of three years from the end of the tax year or one year from the assessment date, with the assessor's value presumed correct for real property.

Taxes on the house are a first lien. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 ranks the tax lien ahead of other liens until actual payment, requires sale proceeds to be applied to taxes and levies, and adds a lien on current-year rents.

The state grantor's tax on a deed is 50 cents per $500 of consideration under Virginia Code 58.1-802, and the seller pays it unless the buyer agrees to. The statute requires the clerk of the court where a deed is first recorded to certify that the tax was paid.

Fauquier County by the numbers

Where is Fauquier County and what is it like?

Fauquier County sits on the Piedmont in Northern Virginia, about 651 square miles of mostly open country with Warrenton as the county seat. The 2020 census counted 72,972 residents, and the Census Bureau estimate for 2025 is 76,503.

The 2020 census counted 26,400 households and a median age of 41.9. Which Fauquier County communities do sellers come from?

Beyond the three towns, Fauquier has a string of unincorporated places that appear on mailing addresses and deeds. The census-designated places are Bealeton, Calverton, Catlett, Marshall, Midland, New Baltimore, Opal, Paris, Rectortown and Upperville.

New Baltimore is the largest community in the county, and Wikipedia ties recent growth to Warrenton and New Baltimore, with the Brookside and Vint Hill subdivisions feeding growth in the east. The census counted 57.5 percent of residents in rural areas in 2020, so land use rules, covered below, come up more here than in a city.

Warrenton and Remington run their own police departments, according to Wikipedia. The county sheriff covers the rest.

How do people get around Fauquier County?

Wikipedia lists Interstate 66 and five U.S. routes among the county's major highways.

  • Interstate and U.S. routes: I-66, US 15, US 17, US 29, US 50 and US 211.
  • State routes: SR 28, SR 55, SR 215, SR 245 and SR 355.
  • Neighbors: Loudoun, Prince William, Stafford, Culpeper, Rappahannock, Warren and Clarke counties.

Wikipedia reports that, as of the 2000 census, 47% of working residents had jobs outside the county, and average travel time to work was 39.2 minutes. Those are older figures, but they explain why many owners here treat the house as a base for a commute.

What do people do for work in Fauquier County?

Local government and health care lead. The county's 2023 financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, ranks the Fauquier County School Board first with 1,000 or more employees.

  1. Fauquier County School Board, 1,000 and over
  2. County of Fauquier, 500 to 999
  3. Fauquier Health System, 500 to 999
  4. U.S. Department of Transportation, 500 to 999
  5. Walmart, 250 to 499

The county is also known for horse country. The Virginia Gold Cup steeplechase has been held in Fauquier since 1922.

Which school districts and colleges serve Fauquier County?

Most of the county is in the Fauquier County Public Schools division. The part on Marine Corps Base Quantico falls under the Defense Department's school system instead.

High schools named on Wikipedia are Fauquier High School, Liberty High School and Kettle Run High School, and the division also runs Mountain Vista Governor's School. Laurel Ridge Community College is the local college. School boundaries can affect how a buyer sees a house, so keep the correct school name in your listing or offer paperwork.

What is the Fauquier County real estate tax rate?

The Commissioner of the Revenue's rate page shows a combined real estate rate of $0.895 per $100 of assessed value. That figure is $0.709 base, $0.182 for the fire and rescue levy and $0.004 for the conservation easement fund.

At $0.895, a house assessed at $500,000 would owe $4,475 a year, or $2,237.50 per half. That is simple arithmetic from the published rate, not a quote.

One special district appears: the Marshall Electric Light and Business Improvement district adds $0.025 per $100. Mobile homes are taxed at the same $0.895 as real estate. The rate page does not carry a date, so confirm the current-year figure with the office when you plan a sale.

When are Fauquier County real estate taxes due?

Fauquier bills half the year in June and half in December. The key tax dates list June 5 for the first half and December 5 for the second half, both paid to the Treasurer's Office, and any date that falls on a weekend moves to the next business day.

  • March 5: renewal for tax relief for the elderly, filed with the Commissioner of the Revenue.
  • June 5: first half real estate taxes due.
  • October 25: revalidation and new land use applications due.
  • December 5: second half real estate taxes due.

Payments and balances are handled through the county's online tax portal, and the Treasurer is Tanya Remson Wilcox. The pages reviewed did not state the late penalty, so ask the Treasurer's Office for the current penalty and interest before you let a bill slide.

How does Fauquier County reassess and hear appeals?

Fauquier reassesses every four years. The last reassessment took effect January 1, 2026, the process carries through 2027, and new values take effect January 1, 2028.

The county's Board of Equalization hears property assessment disputes. The Circuit Court appoints its five members, who must be county residents and a majority freeholders, with at least 30 percent drawn from appraisal, real estate, building, legal or financial work. The ordinance deadline to appeal to the 2026 board was June 17, 2026.

The Commissioner of the Revenue's office is at 10 Courthouse Square, 2nd Floor, Warrenton, VA 20186, phone (540) 422-8880. If the board's result is not enough, Virginia law lets a taxpayer apply to the circuit court. Virginia Code 58.1-3984 presumes the assessor's value, or the board's adjusted value, is correct and puts the burden on the taxpayer to show the value was wrong and not set under accepted appraisal practice.

What land use and tax relief programs affect a Fauquier sale?

Fauquier runs a use value program that taxes qualifying farm, forest, horticultural and open space land on its use instead of its market value. If the land stops qualifying, a roll-back assessment applies, and the county says it requires repayment of the deferred tax plus 10 percent interest for five years plus the current year.

That matters when you sell acreage. Ask the Commissioner of the Revenue whether the parcel is in land use before you agree to a closing date, since a change in use can trigger the bill.

The county also offers real estate tax relief for owners age 65 and older or permanently disabled, with reduction or exemption based on income and net worth, applied for each year. The office number for that program is 540-422-8140.

What happens to Fauquier County tax when the house sells?

The tax lien on a Virginia house outranks other liens until it is paid. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 says sale proceeds must be applied to taxes and levies on the real estate, including penalties and interest, and that the seller's share is prorated by contract.

On the recording side, a deed carries a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 under Virginia Code 58.1-802, paid by the seller unless the buyer agrees to cover it. The Commissioner's office says it keeps ownership records current from deed transfers and other records obtained from the Clerk of the Circuit Court, and asks for timely recording so the right owner is taxed.

Bedford County by the numbers

Where is Bedford County, Virginia, and what is in it?

Bedford County is in the Piedmont region of Virginia, with the town of Bedford as its county seat. It covers 769 square miles, of which 753 are land and 16 are water, and it reaches toward the Blue Ridge.

It borders Rockbridge, Amherst, Campbell, Pittsylvania, Franklin, Roanoke and Botetourt counties, plus the independent city of Lynchburg. Parts of the Blue Ridge Parkway and the Jefferson National Forest lie inside the county, as do parts of the James River Face Wilderness and the Thunder Ridge Wilderness.

The 2020 census counted 79,462 residents, about 106 people per square mile. The population has more than doubled since 1980.

What is the history of Bedford County?

The Virginia General Assembly created the county on December 13, 1753, from part of Lunenburg County, and it is named for the Duke of Bedford. The same page's infobox gives 1754 as the founding year, so the two dates differ by one.

In 1782 Campbell County was formed from eastern Bedford County, and the seat moved from New London to Liberty, the town now called Bedford. In 1786 land south of the Staunton (Roanoke) River went to help form Franklin County, and the present borders were set.

Bedford was an independent city from 1968 and went back to town status, rejoining the county on July 1, 2013. Because the town and the county were once separate localities, ask which office has your parcel on its books if an old document names the city.

What is the economy of Bedford County like?

The county was historically agricultural, and agriculture remains important. Much of the newer housing serves people who work in Lynchburg or Roanoke or who live near Smith Mountain Lake.

Tourism and retail are growing, and some new industry has located near Forest and New London. Well-known places include the National D-Day Memorial, Peaks of Otter, Poplar Forest (Thomas Jefferson's summer retreat) and Smith Mountain Lake.

Some unincorporated areas have mailing addresses in the town of Bedford or in Lynchburg. For a seller, that means the address on a letter may not match the locality that taxes the property, so check your bill for the county name.

When are Bedford County real estate taxes due?

The first payment is due June 5 and the second is due December 5. The county confirmed those dates in a May 2026 notice that said the 2026 bills had been mailed.

The notice also described a billing change. Before 2026, one spring bill carried two payment coupons. Starting in 2026, owners receive two separate bills, one in spring for the first payment and one in fall for the second. An owner who pays the full amount with the spring bill gets no fall bill.

  • Pay online by bank draft or credit card.
  • Pay by mail.
  • Use the drop box.
  • Pay in person at the county office, 122 East Main Street, Bedford, VA 24523.

A spring payment of the full year saves a second trip, and an owner who is about to sell may still want to ask the treasurer which bills have been paid.

That page did not give the tax rate, penalty or interest. Check your bill for the rate, or call the county at 540-586-7601.

What is the Bedford County 2027 reassessment?

Bedford County is reassessing all real estate, and the new values take effect January 1, 2027. The county hired Wingate Appraisal Service, a firm approved by the Virginia Department of Taxation.

Appraisal staff began visiting neighborhoods on March 19, 2025 and were scheduled to continue over 15 months. They view the outside of properties, may take photos for internal use only, and leave a flyer if nobody is home. Their vehicles are marked Real Estate Assessment/Wingate Appraisal Service and staff wear ID badges.

The county said the work would update assessed values to current market value, as Virginia law requires localities to do periodically. It did not state when the last reassessment took place. The county said owners would get reassessment notices in fall 2026. For questions, call the Reassessment Office at 540-587-0745.

How do you appeal a Bedford County assessment?

The appeal goes to the local Board of Equalization. The county's reassessment page did not describe the board or give filing dates, so ask the Reassessment Office what applies to your notice.

Virginia Code section 58.1-3381 requires the board to consider and decide every petition. It may increase, decrease or affirm an assessment, and the owner must be notified before an increase. Virginia Cooperative Extension describes the board stage as taking one to three months.

If the board does not resolve the matter, you can apply to the circuit court under section 58.1-3984. The filing window is the later of three years after the end of the tax year or one year after the assessment date, among other listed cases. In court, the assessor's value is presumed correct and the owner must rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence.

Should you sell before or after the January 2027 values apply?

The answer depends on the number in your notice. A higher assessed value means a bigger bill after January 1, 2027, and a lower one means less. Owners deciding whether to sell should compare the notice to what they expect a buyer to pay.

  • Read the notice as soon as it arrives and note the appeal window.
  • Ask the Reassessment Office how to request a review if the value looks wrong.
  • Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure for the current year before you close.

How are unpaid taxes and transfer costs handled when selling in Bedford County?

The tax lien stays with the property. Under Virginia Code section 58.1-3340, real estate carries a lien for taxes that ranks ahead of other liens until the tax is paid. Sale proceeds go first to the taxes on the property, and the seller's share for the current year is prorated by contract.

Late charges are capped by state law. Section 58.1-3916 limits a locality's penalty to 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest to 10 percent a year. Bedford's own terms were not confirmed, so ask the treasurer.

On the deed, section 58.1-802 sets the grantor tax at 50 cents per $500, paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise. Section 58.1-801 sets the state recordation tax at 25 cents per $100.

Who sells to a cash buyer in Bedford County?

Owners who inherited a house, rent one that needs work, or live out of the area often choose a cash sale. The reassessment, a second tax bill each year and a house that needs repairs can all push that decision.

We buy as is. If you have a Bedford County house you would like to sell, call or text with the address and we will give you a written cash offer.

More questions about Bedford County, VA Property Tax Guide

June 5 and December 5. Starting in 2026, owners receive two separate bills, one in the spring and one in the fall.

When does the Bedford County reassessment take effect?

January 1, 2027. The county said notices would go out in fall 2026.

Who is doing the Bedford County reassessment?

Wingate Appraisal Service, hired by the county and approved by the Virginia Department of Taxation. Call 540-587-0745 with questions.

Is the town of Bedford separate from Bedford County?

Bedford was an independent city from 1968 and reverted to a town, then rejoined the county on July 1, 2013. It is the county seat.

How can I pay my Bedford County real estate tax?

Online by bank draft or credit card, by mail, in the drop box or in person at 122 East Main Street, Bedford.

Where is Alleghany County, Virginia, and what is inside it?

Alleghany County sits on the far western edge of Virginia, in the northernmost part of the Roanoke Region. The Allegheny Mountains run along its western side and gave the county its name, and the whole county lies in the Valley and Ridge part of the state.

It covers 449.7 square miles, and only about 0.7 percent of that is water. The Cowpasture and Jackson Rivers cross the county and come together just south of the boundary near Iron Gate to form the James River. The 2020 census counted 15,223 residents.

The county seat, Covington, is an independent city and is not part of the county. That matters to a seller, because a house with a Covington address can be billed by the city and not by Alleghany County. The largest town inside the county is Clifton Forge, which became a town again on July 1, 2001. Iron Gate and Low Moor are the other communities most often named.

What shaped the local economy and housing stock?

Paper and rail have carried Alleghany County's economy for a long time. WestRock runs a paperboard mill in Covington, described as the second largest on the East Coast, and an extrusion and converting plant in Low Moor. CSX Transportation operates a major locomotive fueling facility in Clifton Forge.

The county's early cash crop was hemp, and farmers later moved to grain, hay and livestock. Iron for the CSS Virginia came from Longdale Furnace in the county during the Civil War. Many present-day residents commute to Lewisburg, West Virginia, to Lexington or to Roanoke.

For a seller, the practical point is that the local job base is small and tied to a few large employers, so the pool of local buyers is limited. A buyer paying cash can take a house as it stands, which some owners prefer to waiting on a financed buyer.

How do roads and rail affect selling a house in Alleghany County?

Interstate 64 crosses the county east to west and U.S. Route 220 runs north to south. Amtrak's Cardinal serves the Clifton Forge station, about 12 miles from Covington.

Because many residents commute to Lewisburg, Lexington or Roanoke, access to the interstate is part of what any buyer considers. Describe your road access plainly when you talk to a buyer.

Who handles real estate tax in Alleghany County?

In Virginia the commissioner of the revenue oversees assessment, and the treasurer collects the bill. Localities may reassess on cycles from one to six years, and the commissioner supervises the work, according to Virginia Cooperative Extension.

Assessments are normally set as of January 1, and an owner who disagrees can go to the local board of equalization. The Alleghany County complex is at 9212 Winterberry Avenue in Covington, which is also the address the town of Clifton Forge lists for written appeals.

We could not open an Alleghany County page that states the current tax rate, the due dates or the late penalty, so we are not repeating figures for them here. The county treasurer and commissioner of the revenue can give you the current bill, the due date and what you owe through the closing date.

How does the Alleghany County Board of Equalization work?

The Board of Equalization hears assessment complaints and can raise, lower or leave an assessment unchanged. The Town of Clifton Forge posted the board's 2025 schedule, with hearings on five days in March 2025 from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm in the Board Room of the county complex.

  • Book a 15 minute slot by calling (540) 863-6640 between 8 am and 5 pm on weekdays, holidays excluded.
  • Or send a written complaint to 9212 Winterberry Avenue, Suite E, Covington, VA 24426.
  • Or appear at the hearing in person, with spoken remarks or written material.

The owner or agent starts with a presumption that the assessment is right. To overcome it, you must show that the assessment is not uniform with similar properties and back that with substantial evidence, or that the property is assessed above its fair market value. Those hearing dates are from 2025, so ask the county for the schedule that applies to the current notice.

What can you do if the board denies your appeal?

You can go to the circuit court. Virginia Code section 58.1-3984 lets an aggrieved owner apply to the circuit court of the locality, and the filing window is the later of three years after the end of the tax year or one year after the assessment date, with other cases listed in the statute.

For real property the assessor's value, or the value the board set, is presumed correct, and the owner has to rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence. Most owners who are about to sell do not pursue a court case, since the sale itself sets the number a buyer will pay.

What happens to unpaid property tax when you sell in Alleghany County?

Unpaid tax follows the house, not the seller. Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 gives real estate a lien for taxes that ranks ahead of other liens, and it stays until the tax is paid to the taxing authority.

At a sale, the proceeds are applied to the taxes on the property. Who bears the current year's share is a matter of the contract, so the purchase agreement should state it. A title company or settlement attorney normally asks the treasurer for a payoff figure before closing.

  • Ask the treasurer for the balance through your expected closing date.
  • Pay the oldest delinquent bill first if more than one is open.
  • Keep the receipt, because the title company may ask to see it.

How much do penalties and transfer taxes cost in Virginia?

State law caps what a locality can charge. Under section 58.1-3916 the penalty for late payment cannot exceed 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest may not exceed 10 percent a year. Each locality sets its own terms by ordinance, so the Alleghany County figure may be lower than the cap.

Two transfer taxes show up on a deed. Under section 58.1-802 the grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of consideration, paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise. Under section 58.1-801 the state recordation tax is 25 cents per $100, and the statute does not say who pays. Local add-ons were not confirmed, so ask the circuit court clerk for the full recording cost.

What do owners in Alleghany County usually face when selling?

Owners selling here can run into a short list of problems.

  • Real estate tax that fell behind on a house that sits empty.
  • Repairs the owner cannot afford before listing.
  • A small local buyer pool, given the size of the county.
  • Uncertainty about whether the address is billed by the county or by the city of Covington.

If any of this describes your house, we can look at it as it is and give you a written cash offer, with no repairs on your side. Call or text and tell us the address.

More questions about Alleghany County, VA Property Tax Guide

Is Covington part of Alleghany County?

No. Covington is the county seat but it is an independent city and not part of the county, so a house inside the city limits is handled by the city. Check your bill to see which office sends it.

What is the largest town in Alleghany County?

Clifton Forge is the largest town. It reincorporated as a town within the county on July 1, 2001.

How do I appeal my Alleghany County assessment?

Contact the county Board of Equalization. The town of Clifton Forge lists (540) 863-6640 for appointments and 9212 Winterberry Avenue, Suite E, Covington, for written complaints. You must show the assessment is above market value or not uniform with similar properties.

Can a buyer take over a house with unpaid property tax?

Yes, but the tax must be dealt with at closing. Virginia gives the tax lien priority over other liens, so the unpaid amount is normally paid from the sale proceeds.

What is the most a Virginia locality can charge for a late real estate tax payment?

State law caps the penalty at 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest at 10 percent a year. The local ordinance sets the actual terms.

Gloucester County by the numbers

Where is Gloucester County, Virginia?

Gloucester County is on the lower Middle Peninsula, with the York River on its south side and the Chesapeake Bay to the east. The county seat is Gloucester Courthouse, and the county is part of the Virginia Beach-Norfolk-Newport News metropolitan area, about 60 miles east of Richmond.

It covers 288 square miles, but only 218 are land, since about 24 percent of the total area is water. Buyers often ask about the water, so expect questions about flooding and insurance.

It borders Middlesex, Mathews, York, James City and King and Queen counties. The George P. Coleman Memorial Bridge carries U.S. 17 over the York River to York County and the Peninsula.

What is the history behind Gloucester County?

The county was formed in 1651 from York County and named for Henry Stuart, Duke of Gloucester, a son of Charles I. The site of Werowocomoco, the capital of the Powhatan Confederacy, lies on the north side of the York River here, and archaeologists confirmed the village site in 2003.

Tobacco farming drove the colonial economy, and several plantation houses still stand, including Rosewell and Warner Hall. Gloucester Point, at the narrow crossing of the York River, was fortified in the 1660s and again in later wars.

One piece of local geography has its own name. The area called Guinea, near Gloucester Point, includes Achilles, Maryus, Perrin, Severn and Big Island, and it was long the center of the county's seafood trade.

Old Gloucester deeds can reference parishes and landmarks that no longer exist, so a seller with an inherited parcel should ask the Circuit Court clerk to pull the chain of title early.

What drives Gloucester County's economy?

Farmland, the waterfront and a commuter link to the Peninsula all matter. Wikipedia describes Gloucester as a retail center around its Main Street and U.S. 17, and as a county that kept large rural areas in the north.

The Virginia Employment Commission list reproduced on Wikipedia names these among the largest employers: Gloucester County Public Schools, Riverside Regional Medical Center, the Virginia Institute of Marine Science, Rappahannock Community College, Walmart and the County of Gloucester. That list is dated, so treat it as a pointer, not a current ranking.

The Virginia Institute of Marine Science, the graduate marine school of William & Mary, is at Gloucester Point on the York River.

How does climate and water affect a Gloucester County house?

With about a quarter of the county's area under water, many parcels sit near tidal creeks, marsh or river frontage. We did not open an official flood-zone page for Gloucester, so we do not give zone numbers; ask the county's planning or building staff, and ask your insurance agent for an elevation certificate if the house is near the water.

Storm history is part of the record. Page Middle School was damaged by a tornado on April 16, 2011, and the school was rebuilt across the street in 2015.

  • Check for moisture in crawl spaces and under porches on low lots.
  • Ask about the age of the septic system and well on rural parcels.
  • Keep any receipts for roof or drainage repairs, because a buyer will ask.

Which schools and parks do buyers mention in Gloucester County?

Gloucester County Public Schools has nine schools: five elementary (Abingdon, Achilles, Bethel, Botetourt and Petsworth), two middle schools (Peasley and Page) and Gloucester High School.

Parks include Beaverdam Park, which sits on a reservoir with trails and boat rental, Woodville Park, Gloucester Point Beach Park and Tyndall's Point Park. The annual Daffodil Festival is held the first weekend in April, and the county calls itself the Daffodil Capital of the World.

Who handles real estate tax in Gloucester County?

The Department of Real Estate Assessment sets values, and the Treasurer collects. The assessment office is at 6489 Main Street, Suite 126, and its number is 804-693-1325. The Treasurer's number is 804-693-2141.

The county says real estate is assessed at 100 percent of fair market value and must be reassessed every three years. Its document list includes a 2026 reassessment and a 2023 reassessment, and the county's staff also lists and appraises new construction from building permits.

The county's own page says assessors use mass appraisal, and that the department does not set market values but reacts to sales and market changes.

When are Gloucester County real estate taxes due?

Real estate tax is billed in two installments, due June 30 and December 5. For 2026 the second installment moved to December 7 because December 5 falls on a weekend.

  • Early June: first installment bills mailed.
  • June 30: first installment due.
  • July 1: 10 percent penalty applies to unpaid first installment bills, and 10 percent annual interest starts.
  • Early November: second installment bills mailed.
  • December 5 (December 7 in 2026): second installment due, with penalty after the due date.

The Treasurer's page puts the 2026 rate at $0.583 per $100 of assessed value. Taxes may be paid in full by June 30, and if a mortgage company escrows your tax, the property owner stays responsible for making sure it is paid.

The county also offers e-billing through an enrollment portal described on the Treasurer's page.

How do you appeal a Gloucester County assessment?

First ask for an administrative review from the Real Estate Assessment office. The owner or an authorized agent files the county's application by the deadline printed on the reassessment notice.

If the review does not settle it, you can file an application with the Board of Equalization, a five-member citizen board appointed by the Circuit Court. The county notes owners may go straight to the board, but most differences are settled at the department level. The last step is a petition to the Circuit Court, and the county gives the Clerk's number as 804-693-2502.

Elderly and disabled tax relief is run through the Commissioner of the Revenue, with an application window that runs from February 1 to May 1. The Commissioner's number is 804-693-3451.

What happens to unpaid tax in Gloucester County?

The Treasurer publishes delinquent lists, and real estate with tax owing for more than two years as of December 31 is subject to sale at public auction under the Virginia Code's bill in equity process. The county names Taxing Authority Consulting Services, P.C. as a firm handling that work.

For a seller, the Virginia Code puts the real estate tax lien ahead of every other lien until the taxing authority is paid, and the lien statute includes penalties and interest. The closing agent pays the balance from your proceeds, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before closing.

What do sellers in Gloucester County usually face?

Owners here often hold inherited waterfront or rural parcels, older homes needing repairs, or houses with tax that slipped past the June 30 or December 5 due dates.

The Treasurer's page lists $0.583 per $100 of assessed value for 2026. Real estate is assessed at 100 percent of market value.

When are Gloucester County real estate taxes due?

June 30 and December 5. In 2026 the December due date moved to December 7 because December 5 falls on a weekend.

The county charges a 10 percent penalty after the due date, plus interest at 10 percent a year on unpaid balances.

Every three years. The county lists reassessment documents for 2023 and 2026.

What is the history of Halifax County?

One piece of local history affects paperwork. South Boston was an independent city through the 1990 census, then became a town again and rejoined Halifax County in 1995. Wikipedia's county article pictures a tobacco barn on Edgewood Farm. The county peaked at 41,442 residents in the 1950 census and has declined since, falling from 37,355 in 2000 to 34,022 in 2020.

How many people live in Halifax County, and what does that mean for housing?

The 2020 census counted 34,022 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 33,447. The housing numbers: 17,275 housing units, 14.9% vacant, and 70.8% of occupied homes owner-occupied.

  • Median age was 47.7 years, and 25.2% of residents were 65 or older.
  • About 33.3% of households were one person living alone.
  • 21.8% of residents lived in urban areas and 78.2% in rural areas.

A county with older owners, many single-person households and a falling population tends to produce estate sales and vacant houses. If you have inherited a Halifax County house you do not plan to keep, the tax bill still arrives every year.

What schools and local government serve Halifax County?

Halifax County Public Schools is the school division. The county is run by a Board of Supervisors with eight districts plus a tie-breaker seat, and it has the usual constitutional offices: the Clerk of the Circuit Court, the Commissioner of the Revenue, the Treasurer, the Sheriff and the Commonwealth's Attorney.

For a house sale, the offices that matter are the Commissioner of the Revenue, the Treasurer and the Clerk, who records deeds.

Who bills real estate tax in Halifax County?

The Treasurer collects, and the Commissioner of the Revenue is the chief tax authority who keeps real estate ownership information. Both offices are at 1030 Mary Bethune Street in Halifax.

  • Treasurer: Suite 103, phone 434-476-3318, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Commissioner of the Revenue: Suite 104, phone 434-476-3314, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The Treasurer's page lists 2026 rates of $0.50 per $100 of value for real estate, $3.85 for personal property and $1.26 for machinery and tools.

Payment fees are posted there too: a 2.50% convenience charge on credit and debit cards, with a $2.00 minimum, and a $1.50 flat fee for eCheck payments.

Real estate tax payments are due June 5 and December 5. For 2026, the Treasurer posted a notice that bills would be mailed after the tax rate was approved on June 1, 2026, and the due date was extended to June 29, 2026.

Personal property and machinery and tools are due December 5. We did not open a page stating the Halifax penalty and interest rates, so ask the Treasurer for them, along with a payoff figure if the house is under contract.

The Treasurer's page also links to a list titled Sale of Valuable Real Estate for November 2026, which is dated 09/23/26 to 10/07/26 in the directory. Ask the Treasurer what that list covers, and call right away if your parcel number appears on it.

What tax relief does Halifax County offer?

The Commissioner's page describes a Real Estate Tax Relief Program that gives a discount on tax bills to elderly or permanently disabled owners who meet income and net worth tests. The discount applies to the house and up to one acre of land.

  • The applicant must be 65 or permanently and totally disabled on December 31 of the prior year.
  • The applicant must own and live in the home on that date.
  • The page lists gross combined income of no more than $22,000, with income of relatives living in the house counted above $8,500.
  • The page lists net worth of no more than $60,000, not counting the house and one acre.

These limits are printed on the county page as posted, and a county can change them, so confirm with the Commissioner before you rely on them. The same office also has forms for a disabled veteran real estate tax exemption and for a land use program.

How do you appeal a Halifax County assessment?

The Commissioner's page links a 2026 Real Estate Assessment Appeal Application, so start there. We did not find a page on that site stating the filing deadline or the board of equalization schedule, so ask the Commissioner at 434-476-3314 how many days you have from your notice.

Virginia also lets a person assessed by a commissioner of the revenue request a correction within three years of the end of the tax year or one year from the assessment date, whichever is later, when the error was the commissioner's or came from a factual mistake in a general reassessment.

How is unpaid tax handled when a Halifax County house sells?

Under the Code of Virginia, the lien for real estate taxes comes before every other lien and stays until the taxing authority is paid. The statute says the purchaser or a foreclosure trustee must see that sale proceeds go toward taxes, including penalties and interest.

At a normal closing, the title company asks the Treasurer for a payoff and pays it from the seller's proceeds. Ask the Treasurer for the figure in writing and check whether the second half is already billed.

What do sellers in Halifax County usually face?

Common situations include inherited farmhouses, rental houses with tenants, vacant homes in smaller towns and houses needing repairs. With 14.9% of housing units vacant in 2020, empty houses are a real part of the local housing stock.

We buy Halifax County houses as-is, and unpaid real estate tax is paid from the proceeds at closing.

Where is Wise County, Virginia, and what is it like?

Wise County sits in the far southwest corner of Virginia, in the Appalachian coalfields along the Kentucky line. Wikipedia's county profile says it was formed in 1856 from Lee, Scott and Russell Counties and named for Governor Henry A. Wise. The county seat is the town of Wise, and the largest town is Big Stone Gap.

The county covers 405 square miles, nearly all of it land, and it lies in mountain country that includes High Knob and Powell Valley. Part of the Jefferson National Forest falls inside its borders. It touches Letcher, Pike and Harlan Counties in Kentucky, and Dickenson, Russell, Scott and Lee Counties in Virginia.

The independent city of Norton sits inside Wise County but is not part of it. For a house in Norton, ask the city's own offices, not the county offices described below.

What towns and communities make up Wise County?

Wise County has six incorporated towns: Appalachia, Big Stone Gap, Coeburn, Pound, St. Paul and Wise. The Census-designated places include Big Stone Gap East, Dunbar, East Stone Gap, Osaka, Riverview, Stonega and Tacoma, plus the campus of the University of Virginia's College at Wise.

Many sellers live in smaller unincorporated communities, such as Derby, Dooley, Exeter, Imboden, Inman, Pardee, Roda and Virginia City. A house in one of those places is taxed by the county only. What shaped the Wise County economy?

Coal has been the defining industry in Wise County since the 1880s, when coal deposits became the dominant resource in the area. The Stonega Coke and Coal Company was formed in the town of Appalachia, and the work drew families from other states and from Europe.

The population peaked at 56,336 in the 1950 census and has fallen since, with a brief rise in the 1970s and 1980s. Today the county's employers include public ones. Red Onion State Prison (opened 1998) and Wallens Ridge State Prison (opened 1999) are both in the county, and Dominion Energy built the Virginia City Hybrid Energy Center there in 2012. The University of Virginia's College at Wise and Mountain Empire Community College in Big Stone Gap add education jobs.

For a seller, the practical point is that housing demand follows local jobs. A house that has sat empty after a family moved away or a parent passed is common, and our team buys houses in this condition as is.

What are the Wise County real estate tax rate and due dates?

For 2026 the Wise County real estate tax rate is $0.69 per $100 of assessed value, and bills are due on June 10 and November 10. The Board of Supervisors sets the rate each spring during budget talks.

As an illustration only, a house assessed at $100,000 would carry $690 of tax for the year at that rate, or $345 per half. Your own assessment will differ, so use the county parcel search for the real number.
