  • A 10% late penalty is added on June 11 and November 11.
  • Interest begins to accrue on July 1 and December 1, respectively.
  • A payment postmarked on or before June 10 or November 10 is accepted without penalty.
  • Not receiving a bill does not remove the penalty or interest.

If a mortgage company pays your tax, the county says it has sent them a request when your tax ticket notes it. Otherwise it is the owner's job to forward the bill.

How do I appeal a Wise County assessment or correct an error?

Start with the Commissioner of the Revenue's office, which maintains the records and answers assessment questions. The county's real estate page links an FAQ on reassessments, so ask the office how often the county reassesses and when appeal windows fall for the current cycle. This page does not state those local dates.

State law gives one route for errors. Under Va. Code 58.1-3980, a person aggrieved by a local tax assessment may apply to the commissioner of the revenue for a correction within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later. For real estate, that route covers errors made by the commissioner or factual errors by others during a general reassessment.

The county also posts forms for land use assessment, tax relief for seniors and people with disabilities, disabled veterans, and surviving spouses of disabled veterans or of veterans killed in action. If you are selling a house that a surviving spouse has lived in, ask whether any relief was applied.

What happens to the tax when I sell a house in Wise County?

Wise County bills the owner on record as of January 1, so a sale in the middle of the year does not by itself move the bill to the buyer. The closing statement is where the tax gets sorted out.

Ask the closing office to check these items with the Treasurer before you sign:

  • Whether the June 10 half has been paid, and whether the November 10 half is open.
  • Whether any 10% penalty or interest has been added to an unpaid half.
  • Who will pay the part of the year the buyer will own, since the bill follows the owner of record.
  • Whether the deed, will or list of heirs for an inherited house has been recorded, because the county uses Clerk of the Circuit Court records to update ownership.

The county asks owners to notify the Treasurer about any change of ownership or billing address. If you inherited a house with unpaid tax, we can often buy it as is and settle the balance from the sale. We make a written cash offer and you decide whether to accept it.

What should a Wise County seller know about schools, roads and daily life?

Buyers ask about commute and schools, so a seller gains from knowing the basics. Wise County Public Schools operates thirteen school facilities, and in 2011 the district consolidated six high schools into three: Union High in the west, Central High in the central and northern parts, and Eastside High in the east.

Major roads are U.S. Route 23, U.S. Route 58 Alternate, and State Routes 63, 72 and 83. Outdoor attractions include the High Knob area, the Clinch River and trails near the Appalachian Trail system.

Summer events include the Virginia-Kentucky District Fair in Wise and the outdoor drama The Trail of the Lonesome Pine in Big Stone Gap. None of that changes how a cash sale works, but it helps you describe the area when you talk to a buyer.

Wise County real estate taxes are due on June 10 and November 10 each year. A 10% penalty is added the next day, and interest starts on July 1 and December 1.

Who sends the property tax bill in Wise County?

The Treasurer's office bills and collects the tax. The Commissioner of the Revenue sets the assessment, and the bill goes to the owner on record as of January 1.

Is Norton part of Wise County for property tax?

No. Norton is an independent city that sits inside the county's borders but is not part of the county, so ask the city about its houses.

Can I sell a Wise County house that has back taxes?

Yes. Unpaid tax carries a 10% penalty and interest, and it should be paid or settled at closing. Call the Treasurer for the exact balance and ask your closing office how it will be handled.

Nelson County splits assessment from collection in the usual Virginia way. The Commissioner of the Revenue handles assessment and the county Treasurer collects.

  • Commissioner of the Revenue: 84 Courthouse Square, P.O. Box 246, Lovingston, VA 22949, phone 434-263-7070.
  • County Administrator and Board of Equalization scheduling: 84 Courthouse Square, phone 434-263-7000, with the Board's appointment line at 434-263-7003.

Lovingston is the county seat. Ask the Clerk of the Circuit Court's office about recording fees and forms before a closing.

What did the 2026 reassessment change in Nelson County?

Nelson County reassessed every property effective January 1, 2026, and the county says it is on a four year cycle. Its reassessment page says the county hired Wampler-Eanes Appraisal Group to do the work in cooperation with the Commissioner's office.

The county cites Va. Code 58.1-3252, which sets general reassessments at every four years, or every three by board vote, and lets counties with 50,000 or fewer residents choose five or six year intervals. Field visits began in fall 2024 and were expected to wrap up in October 2025. Notices of the proposed values were expected to go out in November 2025.

Assessors carried photo IDs and used magnetic signs on their vehicles. They took exterior photos and measurements. An assessment built from exterior data cannot see the inside of a house, so an owner with a damaged or unfinished interior can ask the county what it has on file.

How does the Nelson County Board of Equalization work?

The Board of Equalization hears complaints that an assessment is unequal or above fair market value, and it can raise, lower or affirm the assessment. The county's public notice cites Va. Code 58.1-3378 and 58.1-3379.

  • Deadline: applications for the 2026 session were due April 15, 2026.
  • Hearings: eight sessions between March 2 and March 13, 2026, in the Bridge Conference Room of the Lovingston courthouse.
  • Appointments: scheduled every 30 minutes, booked by calling 434-263-7003.
  • Standard of proof: the taxpayer must overcome a clear presumption in favor of the assessment with a preponderance of evidence of non-uniformity or excess over market value.

These dates belong to the 2026 reassessment cycle. A sale in a later year should rely on the notice that applies then, and the county says additional dates are advertised when needed.

Where is Nelson County, and what is the land like?

Nelson County sits in central Virginia, with the Blue Ridge Mountains along its northwest boundary and the James River along the southeast. Wikipedia lists 474 square miles, of which 471 are land, and a 2020 population of 14,775, with a 2025 estimate of 14,920. The county was created in 1807 from Amherst County and named for Thomas Nelson Jr.

No city or incorporated town exists inside the county. Census designated places include Afton, Arrington, Lovingston, Nellysford, Schuyler, Shipman and Wintergreen. Nellysford is the largest community, and Lovingston is the seat. Adjacent counties are Augusta, Albemarle, Buckingham, Appomattox, Amherst and Rockbridge.

Interstate 64 clips the northern edge, and US 29, US 60, US 250 and State Routes 6, 56 and 151 carry most traffic. Nelson County Public Schools runs two elementary schools, one middle school and Nelson County High School.

What did Hurricane Camille do to Nelson County, and why does it still matter?

On the night of August 19 to 20, 1969, Hurricane Camille stalled on the east side of the Blue Ridge and caused flash floods and mudslides across the county. Wikipedia reports 153 deaths, more than 133 public bridges washed out and rainfall that reached more than 37 inches over five hours in places.

The Tye, Piney, Buffalo and Rockfish rivers all drain to the James, and creek valleys can fill quickly. For a seller, that history is a reason to gather any flood or drainage paperwork for a property near a stream, and for a buyer it is a reason to ask. The county has no city flood office page that we opened, so confirm a parcel's flood status with the county or FEMA map before you describe it to anyone.

What do housing and the local economy look like in Nelson County?

Of 9,871 housing units, 34.5 percent were vacant at the 2020 census, and among occupied homes 78.7 percent were owner occupied.

Recreation stands out in the county's profile. Wintergreen Resort opened in 1975 near Nellysford, and the article counts 12 wineries and vineyards, seven craft breweries and three cideries, plus Crabtree Falls and the Blue Ridge Parkway. A property here can be a mountain house, a farm parcel or a family home, and each raises different tax and access questions.

What happens to tax owed when a Nelson County property sells?

Under Va. Code 58.1-3340, taxes assessed on real estate carry a lien ahead of any other lien, and the buyer or foreclosure trustee must apply sale proceeds to them. Penalties and interest are included, and the treasurer releases the lien afterward. For a portion of a larger tract, the code prorates the tax by the share of the price, and the commissioner can ask for an appraisal when the price looks low.

That tract rule is common in rural counties. If you are selling five acres off a farm, expect the taxes on the whole tract to enter the closing calculation. The seller's year liability is prorated by contract.

Va. Code 58.1-802 adds a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500, paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise, and the clerk of court collects it when the deed is recorded.

Taxes are due twice a year, on June 5 for bills mailed May 1 and on December 5 for bills mailed October 1.

The county page lists Kim Goff as Commissioner of the Revenue at 84 Courthouse Square in Lovingston, phone 434-263-7070.

The 2026 Board of Equalization took applications through April 15, 2026 and held hearings March 2 to 13 in Lovingston. Later years follow the notice the county advertises for that cycle. Call 434-263-7003 to ask about scheduling.

Can I sell Nelson County land with taxes owed?

Yes. Virginia's tax lien is paid from the sale proceeds, and for part of a tract the tax is prorated across the whole tract by price. Ask the treasurer for a payoff before closing.

Spotsylvania County by the numbers

Where is Spotsylvania County, Virginia, and what borders it?

Spotsylvania County sits along the Rappahannock River in central Virginia and borders the City of Fredericksburg. Geographically it is in central Virginia, but its economy and daily traffic tie it to Fredericksburg and the Washington area, and it belongs to the Washington metropolitan statistical area.

The county was formed in 1721 from parts of Essex, King and Queen, and King William counties, and it is named for Lieutenant Governor Alexander Spotswood. The county seat is Spotsylvania Courthouse. There are no incorporated towns or cities inside the county, so the county government handles services and taxes for every parcel.

  • North: the Rappahannock and Rapidan rivers, Fredericksburg and Stafford County, and Culpeper County.
  • South: the North Anna River, Lake Anna, and Hanover and Louisa counties.
  • West: Orange County and Culpeper County.
  • East: Caroline County.

What are the key numbers for Spotsylvania County?

The county covers 414 square miles and had 140,032 residents in the 2020 census, with a 2025 Census Bureau estimate of 155,388. The table below gathers the figures that matter most to someone selling a house here.

MeasureFigure

With a rural third of residents, some Spotsylvania sellers own larger parcels outside the built-up areas. If your property has a private well or septic system, tell the buyer early, since those inspections add scheduling time.

How fast has Spotsylvania County grown?

The county's population rose from 34,435 in 1980 to 140,032 in 2020, more than a fourfold increase in forty years.

  • 1980: 34,435 residents
  • 1990: 57,403
  • 2000: 90,395
  • 2010: 122,397
  • 2020: 140,032
  • 2025 estimate: 155,388

Most of that growth came after 1980, so a large share of the county's housing is relatively recent. Describe your own house's age and updates plainly when you sell, since buyers compare it with homes of its era.

Which communities and mailing addresses fall inside Spotsylvania County?

The county has two census-designated places, Lake Wilderness and Spotsylvania Courthouse, plus dozens of unincorporated communities such as Massaponax, Chancellor, Thornburg, Partlow, Belmont and Brokenburg. Many areas of the county carry Fredericksburg mailing addresses.

That detail trips up sellers. A house with a Fredericksburg address can be taxed by Spotsylvania County, not the City of Fredericksburg, so use the county's assessment search or call the offices to confirm. Fire and rescue come from a county department with 11 stations staffed by career crews around the clock, with volunteer groups adding help on some nights and weekends.

Which roads connect Spotsylvania County to Fredericksburg and Richmond?

Interstate 95 is the main route through the county, and U.S. 1, U.S. 17 and U.S. 522 and State Routes 2, 3 and 208 also serve it.

Because the county's economy ties to Fredericksburg and Washington, how far a house sits from I-95 is a fair question from any buyer. Lake Anna and Lake Anna State Park are among the county's points of interest on its southern side.

How does history affect property in Spotsylvania County?

Four major Civil War battles were fought in Spotsylvania County: Chancellorsville, the Wilderness, Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania Court House. Part of the Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania National Military Park lies inside the county.

Stonewall Jackson was wounded by friendly fire here during Chancellorsville and died days later at Guinea Station. These sites draw visitors, and the county has properties on the National Register of Historic Places. If your house is old, ask the county planning office whether any overlay, easement or review applies before you list it.

What schools and colleges serve Spotsylvania County?

Spotsylvania County Public Schools runs the public schools. Germanna Community College serves Fredericksburg and the counties of Stafford, Spotsylvania, Orange, Culpeper and King George, and the University of Mary Washington is in neighboring Fredericksburg.

Private options include Fredericksburg Academy, Fredericksburg Christian School, The Summit Academy, Odyssey Montessori School, Saint Patrick School and Saint Michael the Archangel High School. Sellers do not need to list school zones themselves, but buyers will look them up, so confirm the zone through the school division.

How can you appeal a Spotsylvania County real estate assessment?

You can ask the assessing office for a review and then take the case to the Board of Equalization. Virginia law presumes the assessor's value is correct, so the owner has to show the home is worth less than assessed or that the value was not set uniformly.

  • The burden of proof sits on the taxpayer, who must prove the case by a preponderance of the evidence.
  • The board may consider sales that happened through December 31 before the assessment's effective date.
  • Studies published after that December 31 cannot be used.
  • The board can raise or lower values to keep the tax burden even.

Errors that the commissioner made, or factual mistakes made in connection with a general reassessment, can be corrected on an application filed within three years of the end of the tax year or within one year of the assessment, whichever is later. Ask the county's Real Estate Assessor for its appeal deadline, because local deadlines vary and we could not open the county's own page.

What if Spotsylvania County real estate tax is behind?

Virginia allows a locality to sell land for delinquent tax once the bill is still unpaid on December 31 after its second anniversary. For condemned buildings, nuisances, derelict structures and blighted property the wait is only one year, and a home assessed at $100,000 or less can also be reached after one year.

Before suing, the tax officer must send notice at least 30 days ahead and publish a list of the parcels. The owner may redeem any time before the sale by paying the full balance, and a partial payment does not stop the case. The treasurer may agree to a payment plan up to 72 months. Heirs who claim ownership by will or intestacy can ask the treasurer to pause a sale.

That last point matters for inherited houses where tax went unpaid after a death. A sale to a cash buyer pays the tax from proceeds, and the treasurer releases the lien afterward.

What does a seller owe at closing in Spotsylvania County?

The seller pays any tax still owed on the property and the state grantor tax, which is 50 cents per $500 of value unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. Unpaid local taxes are a first lien that comes out of the sale price, ahead of other claims.

  • Ask the treasurer for the payoff figure on or near your closing date.
  • Split the current year's tax in the contract so the proration is clear.
  • Give the closing agent the price for the deed's first page, since the clerk will not record without it.
  • The Spotsylvania Clerk of the Circuit Court records deeds for properties in the county.

We did not confirm the county's billing dates, penalty or rate from an official page, so please ask the Treasurer's Office for those before you plan a sale around them.

More questions about Spotsylvania County, VA Property Tax Guide

Is Spotsylvania County a city or a county?

It is a county. Spotsylvania County has no incorporated towns or cities, and the county seat is Spotsylvania Courthouse. The City of Fredericksburg is a separate jurisdiction on its northeastern edge.

Why does my Spotsylvania house have a Fredericksburg address?

Many areas of the county use Fredericksburg mailing addresses. That does not move the property into the city, so county offices still assess and bill it. Confirm with the Commissioner of the Revenue if you are unsure.

How long can taxes go unpaid before Spotsylvania can sell the property?

Under Virginia law, taxes unpaid on December 31 after the second anniversary of the due date can lead to a court sale. For condemned, derelict or blighted property the wait is one year, and a house assessed at $100,000 or less can face sale after one year with a court finding.

Can I appeal my Spotsylvania County assessment?

Yes. You can ask the assessor for a review and appeal to the Board of Equalization, where you must show the value is above fair market value or not uniform. Ask the county for its deadline, since local dates differ.

Who pays the Virginia grantor tax on a Spotsylvania sale?

The seller pays it unless the contract says otherwise. The rate is 50 cents for each $500 of the sale price, and the deed must show the price on its first page before it is recorded.

Where is Orange County, VA, and what is in it?

Orange County is in the central Piedmont of Virginia, covers 343 square miles (341 of them land), and had 36,254 residents at the 2020 census. The county seat is the Town of Orange, and the terrain is rolling hills that rise toward the Blue Ridge Mountains to the west (Wikipedia).

Orange and Gordonsville are the two incorporated towns. Barboursville and Lake of the Woods are census-designated places, and addresses also use names such as Locust Grove, Rapidan, Rhoadesville, Unionville, Somerset and Montpelier Station. Montpelier, the 2,700-acre estate of James Madison, is in the county. Settlement began at Germanna in 1714, and the county was created in 1734 when the House of Burgesses divided Spotsylvania County.

Main roads are U.S. 15, U.S. 33 and U.S. 522, plus State Routes 3, 20 and 231. Orange County Airport and Gordonsville Airport are the two airfields.

Who handles real estate assessment and tax in Orange County?

Orange County has a Real Estate Assessment Department, created in 2024, that sets values, while the Treasurer collects the tax.

OfficeRoleContact on the county site
Real Estate Assessment DepartmentAnnual assessments and appeals intake(540) 672-6173, 112 West Main Street, Orange, VA 22960
TreasurerBills, payments, late payment rulesCounty main line (540) 672-3313, P.O. Box 111, Orange, VA 22960
Board of EqualizationReviews assessment complaintsThrough the assessment department, (540) 672-6173

The county says the department exists to spread the tax burden fairly and that Virginia requires real estate to be assessed at 100 percent of fair market value (Orange County assessment page). For value questions, call the assessment department number above.

When are Orange County real estate taxes due, and what changed in 2025?

Orange County real estate tax is due in two bills, the first half on December 5 and the second half on June 5.

The county moved its tax billing year to match its July 1 to June 30 fiscal year. The board adopted the change on October 8, 2024, under Virginia Code 58.1-3010, and a short interim fiscal year ran January 1 to June 30, 2025. Taxpayers still receive a December bill and a June bill, but December is now the first half (tax year alignment page).

  • September to October: the first bill of the fiscal year is mailed, covering the first half of real estate tax.
  • December 5: first half due, based on the January 1 assessment and the rate set the previous spring.
  • Spring: reassessment notices go out. The county said 2026 notices would be mailed in early May.
  • June 5: second half due. The county's example is that a bill due June 5, 2026 rests on the January 1, 2025 assessment and the rate set in spring 2025.

Reassessment notices are not tax bills. A new value first affects the bill due the following December. That lag matters at closing, because a June payment can be based on an older value than the notice you just received.

What are the late payment penalties in Orange County?

The penalty is 10 percent of the unpaid tax, and interest runs at 10 percent a year on the unpaid tax plus the penalty.

The Treasurer's page says interest on a December bill starts December 6 and accrues on the first of each month afterward, citing Code of Virginia 58.1-3916. Mailed payments count only if postmarked on or before the due date, and a postal meter stamp does not replace a Post Office postmark (late payment page).

  • Penalty and interest cannot be waived because you did not get a bill, the bill went to the wrong address, or you misread the date.
  • An exception exists for a medically determinable impairment on the due date, if payment follows within 30 days.
  • No penalty applies if the lateness came solely from an error by the Treasurer or the Commissioner of the Revenue.

If you are selling a house with a bill that has gone past due, the closing agent will need a payoff that includes both amounts.

How do I appeal an Orange County assessment?

Contact the Real Estate Assessment Department first, file the county's appeal application, and take the matter to the Board of Equalization if the review does not settle it.

The county posts an appeal application and a separate Board of Equalization page. The board is appointed by the circuit court, is made up mostly of local freeholders, and must have at least 30 percent members who are current or former real estate, construction, financial or legal professionals. Its powers come from Chapter 32, Article 14 of Title 58.1 (Board of Equalization page). We could not read the application form, so we leave out its deadline. The notice mailed to you should state it.

State law gives the assessor's value a presumption of correctness and puts the burden on the taxpayer (Va. Code 58.1-3379). Orange County explains that staff do not choose values to change taxes. The value follows the market, and the tax rate is the part the Board of Supervisors sets each spring.

What does a seller need to know about taxes at closing in Orange County?

Real estate tax is a first lien on the property, so it must be paid from the sale proceeds before the buyer takes clear title.

Virginia Code 58.1-3340 makes the tax lien prior to any other lien, requires the purchaser or foreclosure trustee to apply proceeds to taxes, and says the seller's share is prorated by contract (statute). The deed also carries a state grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of consideration, paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise (Va. Code 58.1-802).

Orange County also runs land use and tax relief programs. If the parcel is enrolled in land use assessment, ask the county what happens to the special valuation when the land changes hands. The county's tax pages also list relief for the elderly and disabled and for disabled veterans, and each has its own application.

What do Orange County sellers usually run into?

Sellers in Orange County mostly deal with the timing of the two tax bills and the effect of annual reassessment on the number they see.

  • Parcel size: acreage and land use status can change both the bill and the sale process.
  • Timing: the December and June due dates can fall in the middle of a contract period.
  • Lag: a new assessed value does not reach a bill until the following December.

A direct cash sale can help when an estate wants to avoid repairs, showings and months on the market. The tax payoff works the same way in any sale, so ask the county for a balance first.

December 5 for the first half and June 5 for the second half. The county now bills on a July 1 to June 30 fiscal year, so December is the first bill.

Does Orange County reassess every year?

Yes. The county says it conducts annual reassessments, with the first one in 2025, and mails notices in the spring. Notices are not bills.

Can Orange County waive a late tax penalty?

Rarely. The Treasurer says penalty and interest cannot be waived because you did not receive a bill or misread the date. Limited exceptions cover medical impairment and county error.

Who do I call about an Orange County assessment?

The Real Estate Assessment Department at (540) 672-6173, at 112 West Main Street in Orange.

Taxes owed are paid from the proceeds at closing because they are a first lien. The seller's share of the current year is usually prorated in the contract.

Louisa County by the numbers

Where is Louisa County, Virginia?

Louisa County is a rural county in central Virginia, about an hour's drive or less from Richmond, Fredericksburg and Charlottesville. The county seat is the town of Louisa, and the only other incorporated town is Mineral.

It covers 511 square miles, of which 496 are land and 15 are water. Neighbors are Orange, Spotsylvania, Hanover, Goochland, Fluvanna and Albemarle counties. In the 2020 census the Census Bureau classed every resident as rural.

That 14.7 percent vacancy figure is much higher than in nearby Hanover or Henrico counties. We do not have a sourced reason for it, so if you own an empty or seasonal house here, expect buyers and tax offices to ask about its status.

What is the history of Louisa County?

Louisa County was established in 1742 from Hanover County and named for Princess Louise of Great Britain, the youngest daughter of George II. Before colonial settlement the area was home to the Tutelo, Monacan and Manahoac peoples.

Patrick Henry lived here in the 1760s, and in 1765 he won his first election to the House of Burgesses to represent Louisa. The Virginia Central Railroad came through between 1838 and 1840, and it became a Confederate supply line, which led to cavalry fighting at Trevilians in 1864.

The twentieth century brought two unusual neighbors. Twin Oaks Community, one of the country's oldest secular communes, started in 1967, and Acorn Community followed in 1993. The Green Springs Historic District and Jerdone Castle are among the places the county's Wikipedia entry lists as points of interest.

How did Lake Anna and the 2011 earthquake change Louisa County?

Lake Anna, a 13,000-acre artificial lake, and the North Anna Nuclear Generating Station were built by Virginia Power in the 1970s. In recent years retirees settling near the lake and commuters have driven much of the county's growth, with at least fifteen new housing developments appearing in five years by 2008.

On August 23, 2011, a magnitude 5.8 earthquake struck Virginia, centered in Louisa County about five miles south-southwest of Mineral. Damage in the county topped $70 million.

  • $57.5 million to public school buildings
  • $11.5 million to residential structures
  • $400,000 each to religious and commercial buildings
  • $500,000 to government buildings

For sellers, the earthquake is a useful reminder that a buyer's inspector may ask about foundation cracks or chimney repairs on older houses. Keep any repair records and receipts together, and tell us honestly about past damage so our offer reflects the real condition.

Which communities and roads define Louisa County?

Besides Louisa and Mineral, the county has the census-designated place of Blue Ridge Shores and many unincorporated communities, including Apple Grove, Bumpass, Cuckoo, Ferncliff, Gum Spring, Holly Grove, Orchid, Trevilians, Yanceyville and Zion Crossroads.

Major highways are Interstate 64, U.S. 15, 33, 250 and 522, and State Routes 22, 208 and 231. A local Buckingham Branch freight train still passes the C&O depot and water tower in the town of Louisa. On a rural lot, check how water and sewage are handled and whether a community association applies, and gather those details before a sale.

Louisa County Public Schools serves the entire county as a single division.

How fast has Louisa County grown, and who lives here?

Louisa County had 20,325 residents in 1990, 25,627 in 2000, 33,153 in 2010 and 37,596 in 2020, then an estimated 42,924 in 2025. That is more than double in thirty-five years.

The 2020 census counted 14,921 households. About 27.7 percent had children under 18, 23.7 percent were one person living alone, and 20.5 percent of residents were 65 or older. With a fifth of residents 65 or older, estates and downsizing sales are part of the local picture.

Ask the office what documents the county wants if a personal representative signs for an estate. We have not confirmed those steps on an official county page.

What extensions can the county grant on real estate tax?

The county governing body may by resolution allow reasonable extensions of up to 90 days on real estate tax when good cause exists, and the official who grants one must keep a record. Members of the armed forces deployed outside the United States get an automatic extension on a primary residence until 90 days after deployment ends.

If omitted taxes are assessed, the locality may let the Treasurer set up a payment agreement of no more than 72 months, as long as current taxes are paid as they come due. Whether Louisa County has adopted these options is a question for the Treasurer.

Who handles real estate tax in Louisa County?

In Virginia, a county Treasurer bills and collects real estate tax, and the assessing office sets values. We could not open Louisa County's own tax pages for this guide, so we are not stating the county's tax rate, installment dates, penalty rates or appeal deadline. Please call the Treasurer's office and the county's real estate office to get them.

Ask for these items in writing:

  • Your current balance, with any penalty and interest broken out
  • The next due date and the last day to pay without penalty
  • The deadline and form for appealing an assessment
  • Whether the property is enrolled in any land use or relief program that could affect a sale

What Virginia protections apply to a late Louisa County tax payment?

State law limits what a county can do to a late payer, and Louisa County's ordinance has to stay inside those limits. A penalty for not paying real estate tax cannot exceed 10 percent of the tax past due, and interest cannot exceed 10 percent a year at first.

Several situations remove the penalty altogether:

  • The assessment was made less than two weeks before the due date through the fault of a local official, and it is paid within two weeks of the notice.
  • A payment arrives within five days by mail with a missing or unreadable postmark.
  • The taxpayer shows a Postal Service Certificate of Mailing or other proof of mailing from before the deadline.
  • The taxpayer died or had a medically determinable impairment on the due date, and payment follows within 30 days. A guardian or fiduciary gets 120 days after they begin to act.

Appeals also pause collection. A bill is not delinquent while an administrative appeal filed within 90 days of the assessment is pending, and for 30 days after the decision. The text is in Virginia Code 58.1-3916.

How does a Louisa County owner sell when taxes or repairs are a problem?

A Louisa County owner who is behind on tax, or who has inherited a house that needs work, can sell as is to a cash buyer and settle any tax balance at closing. An heir who takes over a property after a death also benefits from the fiduciary rule above, which gives a guardian or personal representative extra time after they qualify.

Cash Home Buyers can review a Louisa County house in any condition, including one near Lake Anna or on acreage, and provide a written cash offer. You are not obligated to accept, and you can ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure to compare with the offer.

The 2020 census counted 37,596 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 42,924.

A magnitude 5.8 earthquake on August 23, 2011, centered about five miles south-southwest of Mineral, caused more than $70 million in damage countywide.

Can a Louisa County tax penalty be waived after a death?

Virginia law presumes the taxpayer was not at fault if payment comes within 30 days of the due date after a death or medical impairment, and a fiduciary has 120 days after qualifying.

Is Louisa County owner-occupied?

About 80.3 percent of occupied housing units were owner-occupied in the 2020 census, and 14.7 percent of all units were vacant.
